text: Here's a superb place to get a tasty bite before you fly or on your arrival at the Auckland airport.. we've been here twice and both the times the experience has been excellent. The Bagels are yum and made to great taste. If there's something special about this place, it would be it's amazing team and to exclusively mention, Taryn here does a fantastic job. She's an extremely polite and accomodating personality. If you're at this joint and you have her as your host, you're definitely in luck! Definitely recommend this place!

Mcchicken burger was old and soggy. Medium chips was half full, barely anything in the packet. To make the experience even more delightful after purchasing 2 meals for myself and my partner we asked very politely for a paper cup with some tap water as the chips were salty. Staff were rude and a manager came over to say very dismissively we do not give out water here. After spending $30 we’d expect a paper cup full of tap water to be free. awful service (Auckland international departures near gates 1-10). Spend your money elsewhere.
The wonton soup tastes like a cheap instant noodle. And garlic chicken is even worse. I really don’t understand why some people recommend this. It’s terrible.

This is the worst dumpling ever eaten. The Har Gao (prawn dumpling) is hard and soggy. The BBQ pork bun is tasteless. And the Wanton don’t taste anything like Wanton. It has lots of black pepper and starch added.
VERY Overpriced but I enjoyed my Jet Lag Hangover Breakfast of oats and blueberries. Don't like the fact birds are flying around pooping though

6.32am and only one lady was working at the time behind the counter. I cant blame her as she was trying to serve everyone. My food was ready after 16mins My food was a 8 out of 10. I'd like the owners to invest in more stuff so that you can get your bussiness reviews up to standard and food served abit faster. Wish i wont be disappointed next time.

Never buy any food from this kfc. Look how half filled snack box is. I ordered two seperate orders one supercharge slider and one snack box. When i open the box it was only half of the box filled with pop corn and chips and supercharge slider was inside the box. When i asked the staff they are speaking in their language where customers cannot understand. And they said thats the standard. Shame on Auckland air port KFC😡

It's Currently 9.30pm right now and people were getting told they're closed. I went up to ask if they're serving and was told no. I'm sitting here just watching them stack boxes of cooked chicken, boxes of hot chips, gravey, everything into their personal backpacks and shouldering them. I know exactly what they're doing because I've worked in the fast food Industry before. But to see this, in the airport doing this while people wanting KFC is disgusting. To whoever worked on Thursday 15 February 2024, Auckland Airport food court - 9.30pm
Great food for an okay price. Worth the dime compared to every other food place. Service a little slow bc understaffed.

Great laksa, it is mild but you can add more spice if you want. I think it is better this way, than for it to be too spicy as I found in some other places. Yes I got a free jelly drink for this review, but actually, the jelly drink is great as well. I didn't like that the hours on Google maps were not correct and I had to wait 1h till 5 AM unfortunately.

Ordered via self service which crapped out whilst paying. Banking app showed payment but unfriendly rude staff gave 0 f’s and only gave me food when I refused to move from counter without my food or a refund. And to top it off, they forgot my sauce = dry nugs!

This restaurant/bistro is inside Novotel Airport Hotel, If you are staying in this hotel, it's best to opt in for the buffet breakfast, otherwise, there's not much option other than airport food, especially if you are catching an early flight. I like that their breakfast service starts early (530am if I recall correctly?). Their buffet breakfast has a decent spread and options to get started for the day. The food quality is average, perhaps the most disappointing was the bacon 🥓 which is too hard to eat. The environment is relaxing, clean and not overcrowded by tour groups, which is really a plus point. Can't really comment on the service as it was a self service buffet and there wasn't any service staff around.
Cheap price great taste 😜

Best curry in south Auckland. Smoothies are good asf! You can just tell they use fresh ingredients, AND they do halal too! Tried some desserts they have displayed! Guys you have to go and try NOW!! What are you waiting for. 😂
To be honest one of the best and cheapest halaal restaurants in Manurewa ... The food is just so amazing... The customer service was extremely good... Highly recommendable...

I love these takeaways! But today unfortunately I found a fly in my battered oyster batter I'm sure it was just a mistake considering there's alot of flies around nowadays being summer but ya just had to put it out there. Yummy takeaways, yummy batter. Yum fishnchips. Although.

Newly opened restaurant. Very spacious and clean. Staff were all friendly and nice. Food was delicious. Ordered seafood laksa for myself and my family ordered chicken mee-goreng, shrimp nasi goreng, and chicken pad thai (not in picture). Food came fast and hot. Price is reasonable for the serving size of the food. Parking can be hard as there are only limited parking infront and at the back of the restaurant. Would definitely be returning or ordering takeaways next time. Recommended to all.

Tried this new kebab place and was really happy with the food! The kebab was packed with flavour and the sauce options were awesome. I had hummus, mint, and sweet chilli—such a good mix! Staff were friendly and everything came out fresh and hot. Will definitely be coming back with friends!"
We really liked the Non veg thali we ordered in Sab sweets. Very nice shop with lots of options & affordable prices . Yummy food with lovely customer service. 10/10. Higly recommmend !

i just went and orders the two cheese burger meal, i specifically said no cheese on both the burgers and extra pickles on them. When i got the order it had extra cheese and not even one pickle. i did it on the self serve machines as well. so it seemed very spiteful.
The drink was almost completely spilled. All the fries were no longer fresh, which made me feel extremely disgusted.

Unfortunately, my experience with the staff at McDonald’s Manurewa has been disappointing. The attitude of some team members comes across as arrogant, both toward customers and delivery drivers. Even when orders are ready, delivery drivers are often made to wait outside for no reason, which feels unfair and intentional. Good customer service should include respect for everyone, including those picking up food for others. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and works on improving staff behavior and communication.

🍕 Pizza Taste: The pizza was very tasty and fresh. It had a good amount of cheese, and the base was perfectly crispy. 🧑‍🍳 Service: The staff was friendly and helpful. I received my order on time. 🏠 Cleanliness & Ambience: The restaurant was clean and had a comfortable atmosphere for sitting. 💰 Price: The pricing was fair and reasonable for the quality.

Friendly and good value pizza . I recommend order online, phone and deliverly . So u don't have to wait longer or u xan just wait at home. Triple value deal and mega value deal are super super super recommend

Of all the kfcs in nz, I'd say this outlet has the seemingly friendliest staff. All checking up on me to see if I'm alright or need help ordering. I see an all smiles multicultural team working behind the counter. My food arrived fast (Thursday night, 8pm). Seating area is tidy and clean. Keep it up guys!
Yet another great experience at KFC Manurewa. Order was ready before I knew it and staff are very friendly and helpful! Good quality chicken hot and juicey. Fingers were licked it was that good.

Manurewa kfc is the worst ever in auckland.last night bought takeawy from them and gave me half eaten kfc. Manager throwing food on the floor showing of his ego .im not the first on to complain there are many others who got same issue with this kfc.all they need is money but the service is way poor than a road side stall never to buy from manurewa kfc again manager in the photo is very rude and arrogant.
The food was very unhygienic and worst we had order a Rasmalaie there was a hair in the inside in the Rasmlaie bread then told to crew they were ignored

Bought $80 worth of Jalebi for a function and practically got my nose rubbed in dirt with all the disappointment and disapproval...! "Where did all the Jalebi's end up then, you wonder..." well see for yourself...!!

I can understand things are getting expensive these days but this is not fare you can cut down quality and quantity of the food. I already made complaint about this but no result 😢. Apparently its look like smosa dahi chat not smosa chat???? My recommendation to you take another dollar but please make it proper smosa chat.

The cleanest subway. She changed her gloves with new customers and after washing and after any questionable cross contamination. They used to be completely unreasonable with ingredients. If i asked for less meat and more veggies they change me nearly double “for extras” 👎🏻👎🏻 but the attendant today restored my faith all sandwich makers. She was fantastic. Logical and kind at every step. Give her a raise please! I’m coming because of her.

Subway Manurewa was a great spot, well air conditioned and spacious. It's connected to another eatery place, with available carpark (limited). Great staff, friendly and welcoming. Okay seating and tables.
I ordered pizza last night. the quality was very bad and taste was also bad. And your staff is very rude talk. I think they should be educated.

First time ordering from this one. I usually go to the Papatoetoe one which is closer to home but tonight we had a birthday closer to this store. I ordered the x4 pizzas and 1.5L deal. When it came to eating all four of the pizzas were burnt. They were barely touched at this birthday and I am so disappointed that I never checked before I paid or left the store. I never have this issue with the papatoetoe branch. They top the standards and pizzas are never burnt. Please do better rewa.

Ordered the pizza online around 10:52pm Arrived the store around 11:07 pm and they said we did not make the order as the store closes at 11pm. I understand the store closes at 11pm but order got placed online and I received the confirmation. The staff did not have the courtesy to call and let me know that order was cancelled and I had to drive all the way to the store and staff did not even apologise for the inconvenience. Very unprofessional and bad service. Never gonna order from this store and would not recommend to my friends.

Sam and Varun really aggressive and rude customer service in a good afternoon no busy at all that time got 5 minutes late to pick up pizza and it was really cold and when told about it to them they stated blaming me no apology given be them. No manners at all Really cold pizza.

Ordered via Uber Eats and it was so good! Ordered the butter chicken, plain naan and 1 samosa(Got a free one too which was so cool Lol) The chicken was soooooo soft and tender and the sauce was beautiful. The samosa with the wee sauce was my fave! I always drive past this place but never stopped in but now that I know how good their food is, I'll definitely be coming back again! Thank you guys :)

We had a catering for 25 people for our daughter’s birthday. The food was excellent and the quantity was more than enough. Everyone loved each and every dish. Highly recommended Spice star catering for small and big events. Very reasonably priced Special thanks to Ankit who guided me really well throughout on what to order and how much quantity. Well done Team👏
The food was very good. I would recommend everyone to come here and the staff was also very nice.♥️♥️👍🏻

We went admittedly at the end of their day to celebrate my cousins 50th birthday. The chowder was gd after I added shrimp & the calamari. But was not impressed with wat food there was. It looked as though they had served Mondays leftovers. I was with seven others & did mean to complain but have not called. Otherwise the woman at the front of house was very efficient as we dwardled our way in & different people paying etc etc. Was impressed with her efficiency, & how she was able to process everyone separately with eas. Well-done you. The atmosphere suited the room. 3/10. My cousins have been & go frequently as I've seen that heart 💕 that the ladies in my family love as a photo background. The men) boys in our group left us to it, lol. It was a bit cramp and it would have been nice to have a bigger table even though there were only eight of us.

I gave this place a 1 star in 2012 because the staff member cutting up the steak had no business serving customers. This time around, it was so much better. Lamb has become a rarity for buffets, so of course, I went up plenty of times. Food and service was top notch. Happy Days deserves redemption.
The pork belly is the 💣 . It's so great, i csnt stop thinking about it. The Dessert selection is great. This is definitely in my top 3 buffets in Auckland. And the price is 🔥

Not the best place for fish and chips order! Very oily meal! Ordered on the phone today for pickup at 715pm, reached there only to find out they hadn't prepared. And reason they gave was: business very slack today! Wait..What!?? Slack day means they should've remembered my order! And finally when it's done by 730pm, she tells me she'll give me a discount for the error today, in the next order! Ended up, hubby didn't have any work dinner tonight bcoz the fish n chips was too late! That's the last time I go to this place!!
I took a friend there to collect her dinner which was already pre ordered. Service was quick and staff were nice.
Owned by Japanese people, this food is authentic and so good. My favorite was the takoyaki- it tasted just like it did in Osaka.
Delicious, such a cosy vibe in-store too. Authentic food. Definitely going back.

Worst Pizza we have ever had tasted like something you would bring up.4 people only had 1 bit each. We had to order more food as the kids where hungry. Not sure what source they use but I'm sure that somebody there needs their tastebuds tested.

Ordered the meal deal, x2L pizza’s, garlic bread, chips + 1.5L drink. So you actually only get the option of 2 sides🤷‍♂️. It was so hot in there as well. I understand why but damn get a fan yo! Lol Although that happened, I must say I had the best gah damn creamy mushroom chicken pizza i’ve ever had and yall must try it!!🤘😝 Also, my chips were from Select Pizza😅

It's always a delight to have a food with so much of lovely and delicious food. Food made by Inder (Kulwinder), she makes food with so much of passion and joy. Every bite you have, you will vouch and share the story of the meal.

Have had vietnamese salad really a big wow flav 10/10, especially changing it to rice noodles, adding extra meat & bean sprouts. Quality service 10/10 & cleanliness 9/10 Lots of parking easy to walk to with lots of seating & space in the restaurant

My sister and I were craving some Pho so decided to hit this spot in Rewa. We came around 4pm so it was nice and quiet not as busy as the weekend. The service was nice and quick, order at the counter, no fuss. We both ordered the special beef pho and boy it was nice. The flavor in the soup broth was on point 👌 and I like how they are not shy on the meat slices so plenty for the meat lovers 😊. Definitely worth coming again to try the other dishes they have on the menu.

Very delicious and ginormous portion sizes for the price! Each dish came with plenty of chicken and was super filling. Decent food and quick service. Would highly recommend for a quick fix of Viet food 😋

We don’t come to south Auckland often, but this time it happened to be there and we went in. Located on great south road, adjacent to Southmall. Food was ok, better than most of the Vietnamese restaurant here in Auckland. Pricewise definitely not cheap. The combination rice was not enough for me and I had to pay $4.20 for a bowel of rice. That’s quite some. Photos tell a thousand words. You can be the judge

My nanna and I have come here since our move out to Rewa in 2015 and it has never disappointed us. Sadly we moved away but still make that long drive out for this restaurant, that's how good it is. :) The BBQ pork is my go-to, hasn't changed too much outside of costs but that's more or less inflation to blame. Would definitely recommend the pork on rice dishes more than the chicken and duck but to each their own
Nice fresh sushi plenty to chose from and great price. Super friendly service everytime.

Chef is a good friend and I know his exceptional cooking abilities from 2010. This was no exception. Despite being a public holiday when you may expect the weekend's leftovers to be served stale, the first comment from my 7 year old about the fries with the secret seasoning was "this restaurant is good". The red cabbage, coleslaw, pickles, creamed garlic and hummus were fresh too. My only complaint is that I live 30 mins drive away so we look forward to another branch opening soon!
One of, if not, the BEST takeaways in NZ!! The battered mussels are fat and fresh. The fish is perfect. The batter they use is something else. 🤌🤌 Highly recommend it to everyone!!

They have changed their batter ingredients to breadyish batter since about a month ago now! Waste on snapper! Not so great anymore. Been going there for years, changed my f&c Shop, not many left around here. Food quality has dropped a lot and prices have risen. Go find out, you'll see.

Ordered a big order for Saturday pick up. The food was absolutely delicious, fresh, nice and hot, decent portion for price. Staff were so friendly and met the needs of what I was wanting. Amazing place defs worth food here. Food was given on time that was promised. Good business.
There service system has changed. Only one person serving the orders so it's like a doctors office where you wait for hours before you get your order
The food is just so yummy... Everything is so nice and affordable and customer service is so nice... Highly recommendable... Best curries and Chinese food you will ever taste in your life.

So was hearing advertisements about this place on Radio and made me hungry every time I heard it. So I tried it today and I must say it’s not the best! Tried snack food it was ok. Brought chicken curry and rice, lamb and rice. Lamb lacked seasoning and spices only could taste fatty oil. Chicken was 85% cook, very disappointing; could see the raw meat. Both curry was $15 each. Not sure if I wanna try curry again. Want to try the made to order through. On good note was impressed to see Uber was available.

Message for owner only I order Delhi style butter chicken today on uber eats but the flavor didn't quite meet my or any one expectations who know Delhi style butter chicken taste. It was only on the sweeter side, and I personally prefer a mentioned spicier, more robust version. I appreciate the effort put into making but taste was like chicken in sweet tomato puree. Chicken was also not tandoori roasted as Delhi style. Would like to recommend you please remove Delhi style butter chicken from your menu. Because it’s not like 1% of Delhi style. However keema naan was good in taste and worth.

Tried their butter chicken and chicken biryani. Butter chicken was overly sweet like a dessert and biryani was just full of cardamom pods and peppercorns. Both these dishes were inedible for me and my family and we ended up throwing in bin. Haven’t tried these bad food before from any place.

I just ordered a butter chicken swirl on chips and got bbq sauce on chips. I’m so mad it was so disgusting I threw it out after 3 fries. Also the donuts are so dry. Never ordering anything from here again. Whoever works at this place watch your back if I don’t get my refund from Uber eats.

Fuzion Kebab is a great spot, especially since it stays open until 4 AM—perfect for those late-night cravings. Their meat on chips and meat on rice are delicious, and while the fried chicken is a little burnt, I actually enjoy it that way (weird taste buds, I guess). The only downside is the kebab wraps can get pretty sloppy, which makes eating them a bit of a mess. It can be annoying when everything spills out, but overall, the food is tasty. I’d give it a 7.5/10—definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area and need a late-night feed.

This place had a makeover. Smaller counter which feels a bit claustrophobic. They lack in service though. They don't put enough sauce in the burgers yo! Check your burgers before you leave or you'll be bitterly disappointe

Best kfc i have been to. A day ago me and my wife went to buy bucket meal and order was done and as we were leaving my wife saw a staff having her meal which was a salad bowel but we did not know what it was called so we excused her while she was eating and asked her....her name is Resika and she was so nice to us and told us the name of the meal and also the other options we can have.. I really appreciated her for helping us while she was eating........so we went to front counter again to place the order but than I guess it was a new person there who couldn't get what I was asking for and again we asked Resika ...she just left her food and came in to assist us....wow what a great service the kfc staffs give to there customers.... feel so welcomed....

Please give our thanks and appreciation for the wonderful customer service we had from the lady in drive thru tonight between 22.30 and 22.45. she was pleasant helpful and friendly. Last time we went we had a grumpy agro lady that was rude gruff stuffed our order up and generally unpleasant. So it was a breath of fresh air to see someone even so late in the night be cheerful and helpful. Did not get her name but she should be training all the customer service there.

I ordered three snack boxes (two with popcorn chicken and one with chicken nuggets) along with a 1.5-liter Coke Zero from this KFC via DoorDash. The meal was satisfying and filling, though I found the chicken nuggets slightly underwhelming compared to the popcorn chicken. Overall, the food was delicious, and I enjoyed it. I look forward to visiting the location in person to provide a more detailed review in the future.

I ordered a wrap, chicken burger combo, and tenders for takeaway, but it took over an hour to be ready—and they got the order wrong. Unfortunately, my wrap was missing, and the food we did receive was cold, which was really disappointing. That said, we could see the girl serving us was doing her best and trying to stay on top of things.

Be aware of buying from here, the food they serve is not fresh, lack of food hygiene and service, especially being served by the manager. Poor dad, he and i just realised by the looks of the food, it looks like it’s been preheated from day before. Thats just disgusting behaviour, they don’t realise that’s food poisoning, people can get sick and die. The chips looked old and tough, same with the chicken patty in burger, looks like it’s been preheated to the crisp, look so thin and chewy , eew burger buns taste stale, same with the chicken pieces, looks preheated tasted like rubber, yuck. No wonder why hardly any customers come here, very poor standards. If they keep this up, I’m going to forward this to the health department and put a stop to their bad attitude and behaviour in the workplace, same goes with their racial profiling. Disappointed.

Firstly - the fish and chips are wrapped in newsprint paper which is a great start. This is a large and a medium snapper fillet crumbed, and they were huge pieces, with a scoop of chips. A great feed of F&C's and well recommend. Perhaps the chips were slightly on the small size of portion. The only negative was that due to very high demand, there was a long delay between order and delivery, so my recommendation on peak nights is to order well before you need it. The photos show the fillets with a can of coke so you can see the size of the fillets.

Come in to see what it was about, support local Medium chicken kebab on rice - 6.5 / 10 need more meat and salad less rice for $16.50 Egg burger combo - 7/10 burger, pattie made it & salad was fresh 6/10 chips, brown and over cooked Chicken thigh not worth 5 bucks. Was raw, asked to re cook. Was put back in fryer with someone elses order (would of had my syliva and fingers all over it) Average

Really annoyed ordered 3 lunches, paid extra for cheese naans and got plain. Called to say this and I get told no they are cheese, told to bring them back because they don't believe me. Such a same as the curry was good, won't go back, very poor customer service!! Photos to prove I'm not lying!
Absolutely stunning beach. Calm with white soft sand. Lovely wooden decking walkway over the wetland.
Always a favorite place of mine, now made even better with fairy houses and board walks to explore this beautiful park.

A secluded family friendly beach with lovely views. The beach is picturesque and stays shallow for quite a long way out so very safe for younger kids. There are a couple of nice walks which work their way up to a lookout which allows for some great pics. The kids (and most adults) will love the pond that is riddled with a bed of eels. The smallest hint of food will have them chomping for more.

Remote NZ beauty - 100% worth the trip! Disabilty access to toilets, BBQ area, picnic tables, huge grassy space... Beach access via steps or a steep paved path which becomes grass track. NO BINS - please bring rubbish bags and keep this place clean and stunning 🙏🏼🌊🌿

What a great experience. Such a beautiful scene. We went with baby, so did not attempt the walk ways. We walked accross the beach during low tide and went up to the museum. Will definitely head back once baby is a bit older to complete the routes.

What an amazing place! If you want an incredibly picturesque location, coupled with a really cool bush walk, then you need to go check it out! The owners are absolutely lovely, and they maintain the whole place without charging an entry fee. The gift shop is full of some cool little knick knacks, including jars of honey which they make from their own beehives! It's a classic example of a little Kiwi business doing amazing things, so go and give them some love and support. The bush walk only takes about 40 minutes if you do the longer loop, and is relatively easy, helped by ropes on some of the slightly steeper sections, and there's cool little things to explore along the trail

Great museum about the local history of Papakura. Great exhibition with old and new photos comparing the same streets; stories about first settlers etc. Even though the museum focuses on local history you learn a lot about New Zealand in general - the stories about first settlers, land conflicts with Māori native tribes etc. will have repeated themselves everywhere in the country. Highly recommend a visit. Easy and free parking inside the complex which includes a library, coffee shop amongst others. The staff at the museum was super friendly and welcoming too ❤️❤️🙏🏻.

The displays are looking really good lately and it's surprisingly nice inside. I don't know why I was surprised but it's free to go in and it's definitely be worth a look. Next time you're in town just pop on through.
Very interesting place. I had no idea that kauri gum was dug in the area.
I wasn't expecting this hidden gem to be so rich with content. Such good collection with immaculate description and history. Very well maintained and preserved. Kudos guys

Love that it's free! Nicely lain-out and a great collection of things and information signs to represent the town. Only wish there was something else for kids to do... like if they were able to try out the butter churner or sit at the school desk, etc.

Nice little playground with a couple of swings and slide suitable for toddlers. Fully fenced which is a bonus. Trees provided shade but only around the fence. The playground itself is fully exposed to the sun making it very hot especially in the dry heat of summer. Would be nice if our playgrounds gave a bit more protection for our tamariki!
Nice, clean big area enough for everything in mass gathering. Busier nowadays with alot of people using the space to relax & spend time in the area
It's ok. All pretty old. There kids had fun though and the fact it is fenced is good.
Love taken my kids there they have lots of fun

Lovely clean park with a one picnic bench to sit or eat at. A few other spots to sit and relax while your kids play. I would love to see a few more play ground activities for the kids there. Haven't seen public toilets nearby.

View points come on the way, just a stopping point for cars, not more than 2 car spaces here. There is no specific entrance to this place, and it is also very risky to go inside. Slippery and downfall area. Dont try to go down

This is a real oasis of nature and comfort in our city. Every time you come here, you feel the cares of the day dissolve against the background of green trees and the gentle whisper of the wind. Spacious alleys drenched in flowers invite you to take a walk, and many benches offer an opportunity to relax and enjoy the surrounding beauty.
Lovely walk, went as far as I could, thoroughly enjoyed myself. There was even a few bits that reminded me of Silent Hill which was pretty cool
You can park on the side of the road, but just take pictures. It is not a safe place to go down close to the waterfall.
A cool find. Can't swim or anything but it's pretty to walk and climb around
Absolutely enjoy being out in the nature, the track here is well marked and maintained. Amazing scenery and great bird life. Was wonderful and easy moderate hike.

The park is good. There is enough parking space. You can start with a walk and in between you will find multiple look out points to view the fall. The walk is small. there is not enough space near the fall to sit but adjacent to frame there are 5 picnic bench where you can sit with your family and enjoy the lunch. It’s a short trip so you can plan any other landmark to visit. I didn’t find anything interesting here so only 3 star.
Recent updates to park tables and benches. Clean toilets and spacious car park. If you have kids, there's a 25min loop track that you can do. Lots of tracks and camp sites to choose from.

One of the most interesting, exciting, and beautiful places to visit features a dam, a campground, diverse bird species, a suspension loop bridge, and excellent hiking trails. The dam offers stunning views and serves as a striking landmark within the area. The nearby campground provides a perfect base for outdoor adventures, with facilities that cater to both tent campers and those with RVs. Bird watchers will be thrilled by the variety of bird species that can be spotted in the area, making it a prime location for birding. The suspension loop bridge not only offers breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape but also adds a sense of adventure to the experience. Hikers will find a range of trails suitable for all skill levels, from easy walks to challenging treks that reward with panoramic vistas. This destination is perfect for those who love nature and outdoor activities, offering something for everyone to enjoy. Whether you're there to relax in the campground, explore the trails, or simply take in the natural beauty, it's a place that promises unforgettable memories.

The three hour walk is pretty good but lacks signs on several junctions. One path will have lots of uphill steps, the other will have uphill slopes. Take the left path at the first junction to have an easier loop.

Just visited Hunua Falls with family and a few friends, what an awesome spot! It’s a bigger than usual NZ waterfalls and super impressive, even though the water was brown from the rain the day before. Still, the whole place has a really peaceful vibe and it’s amazing how close it is to Auckland. Would’ve been perfect if the weather was sunny and dry we were hanging out for a picnic right next to the falls! But even with the damp ground, there were some great seating areas around for picnics or just chilling out. Definitely worth the short drive. Loved it, and will be back for sure (hopefully with sunshine next time!)

A peaceful spot, perfect for a relaxing day out. The falls is stunning, and the area is well-maintained and can have a dip. Visited on perfect sunny day. Can walk up to the bottom of the fall. The walk up to the upper lookout is easy and has breathtaking views. If you look out carefully, you’ll see a Waka Hotel which is lovely and quite interesting. Definitely recommend to anyone looking for a scenic getaway. Children friendly.

A must see if coming to Auckland, such a beautiful place to go for a trek along the different trails, or a quick dip to cool off on the hot days we have here, the waterfall is beautiful and such a nice backdrop for the family photo. Can get busy during the weekends so may have to park up the drive down and walk down, a fairly easy gradient too.

The way going there too far from west Auckland. Take me 1hr driving but it’s worth it. I love going there. Don’t need to walk so far to get to waterfall. The toilet is so clean better than other waterfalls that I went before. Can picnic there with your lovely family.

The Stairs of Empowerment, located along the path leading to Weymouth Beach from Palmers Road, were once a symbol of community pride and youthful positivity. Originally painted by local rangatahi as part of the Manurewa Junior Youth Spiritual Empowerment Programme, the steps were meant to inspire with words like “courage,” “unity,” and “hope” decorating each riser in bright, vibrant colours. Unfortunately, time hasn’t been kind to the installation. The paint is now faded and chipped, and weeds have begun to creep back through the cracks. While the effort behind it was admirable, the result today feels more like an abandoned project than a proud landmark. The surrounding area doesn’t do the stairs any favours. Weymouth Beach itself is in rough shape, especially after it rains. The shoreline becomes muddy and often littered with rubbish that washes up or gets left behind. There’s little in the way of maintenance, and signs of neglect are everywhere — from overgrown grass and uneven walkways to broken bits of fencing and worn-out signage. It feels as though this entire stretch has been overlooked by the council for years. Adding to the problem is the sheer number of unleashed dogs in the area. Despite signage asking for dogs to be leashed, many owners let their pets roam freely, and not everyone picks up after them. This makes walking through the park and along the beach unpleasant, particularly for families with young kids or those simply hoping for a peaceful stroll. It’s not uncommon to come across dogs running through the bush or splashing in the muddy shallows, with no one in sight to control them. There’s no doubt that the Weymouth coastline has potential. The location is beautiful on a clear day, and the sense of community spirit is still felt in small ways — especially when you consider that local youth once took the time to transform an ordinary staircase into something meaningful. But right now, the beach and its surroundings need serious attention. The Stairs of Empowerment could become a true local icon again with some refurbishment, but without proper care and investment from the council, the area will likely continue to decline. What should be a peaceful, welcoming spot for locals and visitors alike has become rundown and poorly maintained — a missed opportunity that deserves better.

Donald McLean Lookout is an amazing stop to get a very good view of the city from a very different perspective. There is easy parking within 20 minutes of the summit or you can access several longer versions by parking at either the Whatipu beach end and walking north east along the ridge line on the Omanawani track accesses or park closer to Huia and access from the Puriri Ridge track. Respectively these take about 1.5 to 2 hours the longer period if you stop to take in some of the views along the way. The tracks are all in great condition currently easy walking but worth taking a day pack with plenty of water and warm clothing if you get caught out in a sudden rain event. Sudden rain events can readily happen depending on the daily weather forecast. The area can generate it's own weather events that are outside of normal forecasting for Auckland. Therefore worth being prepared. From the Huia end of the Piriri Ridge track is a water fall that is nice for a dip in to cool off. It has resident eels and fish species that are all protected so observation only for everything in these locations. The surrounding area is rich in history of days gone by from when we didn't understand what high intensity logging would do to the environment so it is special to see the giants slowly returning to a natural state and to be able to get in amongst it all in this way. There is no wheelchair access along the tracks and plenty of stairs in the lower longer routes. From the top carpark you could access with special needs to the viewing platforms if you have help and take your time. So go and enjoy one of Auckland's special places and take home what you take in.

We entered Totara Park from Everglade Drive, a quiet and convenient access point that immediately immerses you in nature. The moment we stepped onto the track, the sounds of the city faded away and were replaced by birdsong, rustling leaves, and the occasional splash from hidden creeks. The path was wide and well-maintained, winding gently through native bush and shaded by tall trees that offered welcome relief from the sun. As we made our way deeper into the park, we came across several junctions leading to different walking and biking tracks. Signage was clear, and the trails varied in difficulty, catering to everyone from casual walkers to more experienced hikers and mountain bikers. We followed a relatively easy route, enjoying the serenity of the forest and the occasional open meadow where families were picnicking and children were playing. Eventually, we reached the highlight of our walk — the Totara Waterfall. It’s not huge, but it has a calming presence, tucked into a quiet corner of the park and surrounded by dense greenery. The water cascades gently over rocks into a shallow pool, creating a peaceful scene that feels far removed from the busy suburbs just beyond the trees. It’s the kind of spot that makes you want to just sit and breathe it all in. After spending some time near the waterfall, we continued exploring the park and stumbled across more hidden gems — wooden bridges, boardwalks, and small clearings perfect for a break or a photo. The loop brought us back to Everglade Drive with ease, making the whole experience feel like a mini adventure. Totara Park is more than just a green space — it’s a sanctuary tucked within Manukau that invites you to slow down, reconnect with nature, and discover something new every time you visit. Entering from Everglade Drive was the perfect starting point for a relaxing and memorable day out.

We paid a little extra for train tickets, which loops around the park and of course, all the kids love it. From mythical creatures to dinosaurs, there really is something for everyone. We were also really impressed with the shade covers throughout the park, as so many places don't consider this. A great family day out and highly enjoyable.

Butterfly Creek is such a fun day out for families — especially with toddlers or preschoolers. It’s one of those spots where you can easily spend half a day or more without running out of things to do. The butterfly house is genuinely beautiful — warm, tropical and full of colour. Butterflies fly right past your face (or land on your pram!), and there are turtles, fish and little birds to spot too. It’s humid inside so dress in layers, but it’s a magical experience for young kids and adults alike. The train ride was hands-down the biggest hit. Short and sweet, but exciting for little ones — it loops around the dinosaurs and gives you a mini “tour” feel. You can ride it more than once if your child’s obsessed (like mine). Outside, there’s heaps of space to run around, shaded seating areas for picnics, a decent-sized playground, and a cafe with both indoor and outdoor tables. We found the layout super manageable with a stroller, and the whole place is very pram-friendly. TIP: Get there earlier in the day so you can pace yourself — there’s a lot to explore between the butterflies, farm animals, playground, train, and dino trail. Bring snacks and water bottles if you’re staying for a while. Parking is easy and free, right outside. Would I recommend it? Absolutely — a great mix of animals, play, and nature that works for all energy levels. Ideal for a toddler adventure day or a relaxed family visit.

Butterfly Creek was absolutely awesome! 3 year old can't stop talking about it! Great value for money and so much fun. Plenty of parking, super kind and helpful staff. We took a wheelchair around too and it handled most of it really well. It was such a fun and underrated place. We can't wait to be back!!!

Real live kiwis for those who want to see some. Small in size but still worth a visit. Restaurant/cafe and gift shop on site. The train ride is packed. I recommend skipping it and just doing the walk. Close to the airport. Good for tourists staying close to the airport. Perfect for dads to bring kids to enjoy while mom shops at the outlet.

Great experience had a one-on-one session with expert and his scope. Very accommodating over time/location and easy to organize. Found a venue in a park in South Auckland with reasonable city viewing. Tour consisted on introductory hot drink, overview of night sky viewing then a carefully curated look at stars, nebulae, saturn and neptune with interesting expert commentary. Very highly recommended.
Loved it! Interesting and cosy, like having a planetarium tour at home.

Rainbow’s End was a fantastic day out. We were visiting from Australia and were able to access everything. It wasn’t too busy and we were able to do all the rides we wanted PLUS go on the Cork Screw 4 times in a row 🤣 it was by far my favourite. Food was available and reasonably priced. Staff were friendly and available to help when needed too. Ice cream choices were hectic to choose from and a bonus day with UV reactive face painting. Absolutely brilliant day and will definitely tell friends and family to go along too.

Super cool, loved the themed rides like "Gold Rush", as well as the fear fall, my personal favorite was the "Invader". While I didn't get the opportunity to ride the Stratosfear I've been told its incredibly fun, however the lines are long as you'd expect.

Our family with toddler totally enjoyed the rides. It was also a great deal given the huge discount for weekday passes. Parents of older kids that do not wish to play cld also buy spectator passes to save some money. There's a good amount of rides that the young one above 90cm cld ride including bumper cars and roller coasters. No queue too on a weekday. The whole place also has plenty of clean bathrooms and seating, almost spotless. Only minus is that there's few food options and the park doesn't allow outside food and drinks.

Great place to take the family for themepark rides. Food is mm ok, definitely check out the Gold Panning area, great way to Pan for Gems & crystals. Rainbow Candy is awesome 👌 some rides do need more padding on back seats 😅 you may get a sore back Worth the money for the days fun

Great time with the family. We had a great time and was able to all but one of the rides (due to maintenance being performed on the ride, we were informed of this before entering park) Food was expensive but expected. Was able to enjoy a full day there with the family.

Amazing experience for a birthday party for a bunch of teens. The guides were knowledgeable and so friendly and helpful. The kids had a blast. The caterer was also so friendly and accomodating. The pizzas were delicious! The vegetarian pizza was incredible, highly recommended. Everything from the staff to the facilities to the activities were bang on. We’ll definitely be back 😊
Absolutely great family fun day! Instructors were friendly & clear communication with safety for each of us was paramount! Highly recommend to all!

My family of three, which includes a 9 year old, loved this event on vacation!! Two hours was plenty to learn time be safe and try the rapids several times. Options were available for swim levels to drift downstream. Our guide, George, was amazing and persistent with the three children in our raft without being harsh. Video is purchased separately for your experiences. The changing area is large and clean.

I did white water rafting at Vector Wero for my hens party and we got the most wonderful, fun and competent instructor, Bree. She took care of us so well and made it such an exceptional experience. Highly recommend. And Bree, as promised here is a few pics of the wedding dress!

Amazing team event for a croud of 40 people. Very well organized. We had people varying in age from 5-55 and all of them had the greatest time. The team was amazing and full of energy and ebsured that we had a great time. Would surely recommend for any team building events.

The route is a bit confusing but it’s a good park if you wanna stay there for a full day as it has heaps of stuff to do. You may visit the AKL Botanic Gardens, walk around the path and go to the scenic lookout. Oh you can also unleash your dog in a huge area.

Best viewpoint available in Manukau area I reckon. Beautiful spot to setup for a picnic with the botanical gardens and Totara park nearby. Gates are always closed to vehicles but can walk to summit any time of the day.
What a fantastic view! Loved seeing all the adorable walkers and their cute doggies from the community.
The highlight of this area is the path flanked by tall trees, where a fantasy walk truly comes to life. It's a magical experience, offering an escape into a world of wonder and beauty.
One of the most beautiful and picturesque spots. Will visit each time when I'm in Auckland.

Awesome experience for all ages. Its not just for kids! The tower is 4 stories high, I chickened out at the top and went down a level. Whats great about this place is you choose your path. You choose how high to climb, and at each platform you have 2-4 choices of where to go next. So no getting stuck behind someone. The obstacles have 3 levels of difficulty and they are colour coded so you know what you are getting into. The talk, harness and lesson at the start take a while but once you're up there you have plenty of time. One suggestion I'd make is that the staff could wear different colored helmets so we know who they are! They were very helpful
So fun!
I go to Murphy's Bush with my dog after taking her to the vets. This time l also took my friend. Poppy loves to have a sleep after we have lunch.

Relatively small reserve but with quite breathtaking scenery tucked inside, without telling where it is, the picture look like as if it's taken from some bush walk in the Coromandel, locate at the centre there is an open space with a few picnic tables, toilet locate near the entrance.
Fantastic place to visit, a must go....

Very nice, clean and quite place in the middle of busy area. Can see and feel the nz bush preserved and the path made are really good, can't get lost and the arrows shows which way to go. Just love listening to the birds and nature.

Great walk in the bush. You would never guess you were in the middle of a city. Dog friendly, easy walk for kids or the more elderly. Or a good area for a jog. Smack in the center is a wonderful picnic area. Highly recommend
Nice but short walk and lovely picnic area just a bit muddy after all the rain would be lovely when a bit dryer

Really cool forest full of ferns. No trails where I entered and a little swampy in some locations but very doable. A cyclone went through the week before so maybe that had an effect. Love this place. Not far from home and a lovely walk around when you feel like being with nature in the bush. .
Bush walks are great on a sunny day, track needs a little more maintenance, lots of broken brunches and paths need a little tidy up but safe enough to walk

Still like this place. Should have come earlier as I missed the bread. Had yummy juice and whitebait fritters. Seems to be more food and less of the local growers compared to 10 years ago. Bought some lovely cherry tomatoes and some clementine. Was hoping for some nuts.

The best place to go on a Sunday… loved the chocolates and food there . But I missed the fresh pasture raised eggs the lady was selling .. got it once but then never saw her again. The brookewood chocolate was very good! Not too sweet n get the right balance. Thai food in the kitchen area was good value for money and delicious. Will def go back again

A market that’s actually fun to spend time in with great high-quality products and food. Compared to other markets that are just hustle and bustle, leaving hungry - the food here is great. Smoked fish from Clevedon is a must!

A beautiful and well-kept scenic reserve. The steps along the track are in great condition with no slippery sections, making the walk safe and comfortable. The amenities are clean and well maintained, which is especially appreciated by regular visitors. The hike takes roughly an hour to go up and return, depending on your pace. I absolutely loved this gem of a place. It easily rivals the historical places closer to the city, with its park like grounds, plenty of off road parking & the volunteers who run it shared the history of the place. It was wonderful to see the huge old trees, & the old fruit trees as well, with the farm machinery & everything you’d need for survival on such a place. It’s Well worth a visit, & there’s a lovely cafe within a 5 minute drive in Clevedon

An out-of-the way museum with a very assorted collection on display. Several rooms are open that are roughly as follows: education and technology (so that has typewriters and cameras and radios), a household room (kitchen, laundry, medicine cupboard items), war (world wars and Scouts), sports and community, bedroom (items from assorted eras). Plenty of local photographs, some of which are photocopies, line the walls. Very modest entry fee of $3. Limited parking, but as there are so few visitors it seems not a lot is needed. Some items on display in the sheds or stable/garage but don't appear to be organised. No wheelchair entrance or path to the door. Most of the displays are upstairs so you have to be mobile enough to manage stairs. Staffed by informed volunteers and members of the local historical society. Well worth talking to them to walk you through the displays and for background information.

I used to maintain the outside area' for the council a few years back. It has history! "the place' especially with no one around has got that eary quiteness about it" a cool place, the long drop is a blast from the past too, classic old school!! Worth a visit if your in the area"

Volunteer run museum and historic homestead detailing the history of the McNicol family and of the Clevedon area. Personal introduction of the homestead and history of the area given by Phil upon arrival. Spent over an hour there looking through the various displays, photos and materials.

Not very much to see, but a well-informed docent and a lovely little house with a decent collection of local history. A bit eclectic and not very clearly organized. But there's a clear passion for the area, and it's well-cared for.
Thank you Adam for an awesome first-time canyoning experience!! The waterfall was beautiful and very powerful! It's so fun and exhilarating to abseil down the Kitekite falls in Piha.

Had an awesome time! We’d done some canyoning before, and Cam was a legend at making this experience fun and engaging for us. Route was well equiped and safety was a top priority. Would recommend as a must do for first time canyoners, or anyone looking for a great activity close to Auckland!

Fantastic organisation and experience! Our guide, Adam was really good. He talked through all the safety stuff, he encouraged us through the tricky bits, and got some great photos through the fun bits on the way down Piha canyon. Thanks again, Adam! Jed and I had a great time!

Awesome experience to get to repel down a waterfall and then hike through, crawl through, and swim through the canyon to get out. Our guide was very nice and incredibly knowledgeable about the local plants and animal species. Our only regret is not doing the full day tour to repel down the really big waterfall!

Absolutely incredible experience!!! We have never done abseiling before but have been around the climbing scene and enjoyed ourselves so much. They instruct you through everything you need to know and have alternatives for if you’re too scared for anything. They are so encouraging and helpful and is one of the best guides we’ve ever been on. Adam was our guide and he was such a great human with a heart of gold. With easy pick up from hotels to driving us and keeping us encouraged and safe. Adam is such an amazing and awesome guy and you’d be more than lucky to get him as your tour guide. Thank you guys so much for the awesome day with great memories!

This serene pool is perfect for wading at low tide. Piha's renowned surf is buffered a rocky barrier rising up from the beach. It is fun to watch the tide come in as the surge blasts it's way through and over the rocks.

Must go during low tide! The hiking trail from the parking lot up to Tasman Lookout is washed out. The only way to access it is near the blue pool - up and back. Beautiful sights with a sparkly black sand beach.

Very fun little swimming hole at low tide. Actually gets pretty deep in some spots, but be careful of rocks that are sharp at the bottom. It warms up at the peak of low tide but as the waves start coming over as the tide rises, it gets cold.

The Blue Pool is a collection of tidal, salt water pools at the southern end of Piha Beach. The area is unique and beautiful! The pools are formed in an area behind a gap (known as “The Gap” by locals) in the rocks between Taitomo Island and the southern shore, which provides a good wave break and protection from the rough ocean. The Pool is mostly shallow, but gets deeper at high tide, and is very deep in the center where the waves crash over the rocks. It is very popular with locals and tourists alike as a great place to relax and swim with some protection from the rough surf. It’s a good place for kids to play in the water, without the risk of the rough waves, but there are no lifeguards on this portion of the beach. Because it is tidal, the water is deepest and the pool is much larger at high tide. Just be aware that it is more difficult to get to the pools when the tide is at its peak. (See explanation below) The surrounding beach area is bounded by rocky hills, so it affords more privacy than the large, open beaches. There are a few shaded areas to relax in along the edge of the rocky cliffs, but be careful to watch for falling rocks. It can be busier on weekends or holidays, but on many weekdays, we have been the only couple lounging there! Remember that the beach here is just like Piha Beach- black sand... So, the sand gets hot in the sunshine! Wear beach shoes or sandals, and take a large beach towel with you. There are no restrooms on this area of the beach. The closest ones are at the south Piha Beach parking area. It is easy to get to the Pools at low tide by just walking along the southern end of Piha Beach towards Taitomo Rock. You will continue along the beach until you pass the natural tunnel (called “The Gap” by locals), then you will see the Blue Pools to your left. At high tide, when the beach access route is obstructed by waves, the best way to reach the Pools or return from the Pools is to use the trail that accesses the Tasman Lookout. If you start from the south end of the beach parking lot, just find the trail near the turnaround and take the trail up to the lookout, then keep going past the lookout. The trail will go along the ridge, then turn down to the beach so that you can access the Pools. If you are at the Pools when the tide comes in, you are not trapped! Just walk to the southern end of the enclosed beach area to find the sign for the trail to the Tasman Lookout, and take that trail back to the parking area. The last thing to know is that the south parking area for Piha Beach is often very crowded on weekends or holidays, and on weekdays it can be crowded around the popular surfing times or sunset time. If you can’t find parking, drive around to the grass parking area adjacent to the Bowling Club (on the left past the campground and Piha Store), then walk across the bridge to access the southern part of Piha Beach
Wow. Just wow
Wave power...Awesome
Great rocks where the surf is raging. About 5 minutes from left Pia Beach.

Great walk, the views are stunning and worth the drive. I’d recommend getting there by 10:30 for car parking. We did go on Mother’s Day so others days might be better. There is a restroom at the car park. Suitable for most ages over preschoolers. Not stroller friendly

This is a super cool track. Yes you can bring your furry friend, please keep them on leash as there are some big drop offs and falls off the pathway. This is a well maintained path, its gravel and dirt the whole way. The track is an up and down loop walk and maybe challenging depending on your fitness level. Don't fret there are so many nice places to stop and take in the scenery it would be a waste to rush through. There are some spectacular views so much so that you need to fight for a photo spot, go during the week if possible. There is one toilet (long drop) in the car park but none on the trails.

Beautiful mild walk that takes around 40mins to 1 hour to complete. Great views and a couple of info boards about the historical Pa site on there, which was interesting to read. I went with my 3 kids (7, 5 and 3) and managed to do it in an hour or so (one cried on the way back as she isn’t much of a hiker 😅). Not much shade on the trail so best to go early mornings or late afternoon

Gorgeous views! Fairly easy trail to hike but somewhat steep in some spots so take care! Easy access to the car park as the road is paved and there’s only few hundred meters of gravel road towards the end.
Awesome view point. Great walk through nature..
Excellent view point for walking Need a good shoe to walk. Not a city shoe or office shoe.
Nice easy walking, take the kids.
A variable track, great for families with outstanding landscape.

Great walking track around Mercer bay loop. Shame the track to Kerekere beach is closed from Iwi Rahui from Kauri die back. Difficult to understand that one when there is no Kauri on the walk! Would be good for Iwi to pay for some better tracks so our kids can learn more about the outdoors. Isn't that the idea of being a good custodian of the land. Denying access to our resources is not protecting them.

The Keyhole is a natural tunnel made by geologic features and erosion through the eastern end of Taitomo Island. It is a popular place for photos, and for lounging in the swimming hole adjacent to it. When the tide is coming in, or the waves are high, the water crashing through the Keyhole can be spectacular. Be very careful near the opening if the waves are rough, and it’s better to not try to venture inside. To get to the Keyhole at low tide, just keep walking south on Piha Beach until you pass the Tasman lookout and you will see the island and the Keyhole on your right. If the tide is up and the beach access is blocked, take the trail at the end of the south parking area for Piha Beach up to the Tasman Lookout, then just keep walking past the Lookout until the trail winds back down to the beach. When you reach the beach, you will first see the Blue Pool and the Gap. (Another nice swimming place) Walk to your right towards Taitomo Island and you will see the Keyhole
