Great, secluded little spot for kids to play. Gentle (if any) waves.
Stunning!
I love there 💖
Only go during low tide! The hiking trail to the lookout from the parking lot is washed out. Great views and worth the effort!
Lovely beach area. Nice beach to walk on.
A beautiful scenic Lookout point above entry to Piha & beach

Sparkling sand and gravity defying rock face! This is a place to visit, the water is warm and there is a beach cove off the main swimming beach. Sand sparkles like little diamonds and the cliff next to the beach with its suspended rocks is spectacular, photos do not do it justice. Take your own drinks and plenty of snacks for the day as there is no close shops. There is a restaurant if you fancy a quick bite.

A “must-do” little hike for the views up to Tasman Lookout when you visit Piha Beach. It’s only 20 minutes or less up the trail from the end of the parking lot on the South end of Piha Beach to the lookout. Beautiful views from there of the beaches, the ocean, the town of Piha and the surrounding mountains. You can also see the Gap and the Blue Pools from here. It’s an uphill hike to the lookout, but the trail is easy and anyone can do it. You can hike one way from the parking area, or the other way from the beach at the Blue Pools. If you hike from the parking lot, just keep hiking south past the lookout, and you will find the trail down to the beach, the Blue Pools and the Gap. All great places to see and a beautiful place to relax and soak in the water. At low tide, you can continue walking along the beach at the Gap, and around to the southern part of Piha Beach

Scrambled our way up the rock, there are stellar views of piha up top! trail is pretty easy to find, but some parts are made up of sand so caution is necessary antigravity rocks are a bit harder to get to- scramble down at the end of the track but be careful as there is a steep drop!

Watch the powerful Tasman Sea surge into natural rock tunnels, creating impressive plumes of water – a fantastic photo opportunity! Enjoy invigorating coastal walks with stunning ocean views. Good to know for your visit: The exposed rocks can be sharp, so wear sturdy footwear. Due to the potentially hazardous terrain and the nature of the blowholes. Really wouldn't advise swimming in this area, head around to the Blue Pool Getting there involves a scenic drive from Auckland. Be aware that parking can be limited, especially during peak times. While not a swimming beach due to the rugged coastline and powerful waves, Taitomo Rock provides a thrilling display of nature's power. It's a unique and memorable coastal stop.

An easy walk here from the southern part of Piha Beach. This area of the southern beach is best known for two local sites: The Keyhole (a natural tunnel), and the Gap and Blue Pools. You can easily reach both at low tide by walking along south along the water from Piha Beach. If the tide is high, use the trail from the south parking lot to hike up to Tasman overlook, then just keep hiking south past the overlook until the trail heads back down to the beach and the Blue Pool. The Blue Pool is a great place for laying in the sun in n the beach that surrounds it, and a nice place for soaking and swimming, too. The beach here is also usually less crowded and more private than the main beach area, and is sometimes somewhat sheltered from the wind. A “must see” when you come to Piha!
You can view the best of nature here, super big waves and an awesome opportunity to observe the tides during one day.
A short rock walk up the point with goat trakcs and sheer cliffs. Not for the faint hearted, but very cool at the top.
Beautiful beach- especially at low tide! No toilets or showers, but very nice view
Beautiful beach. Very good view from the view point
A lovely view of a beauty of a beach! Popular for surfing! Cute restaurant!
Such a vibe. Stunning sunset from the shore or any of the high lookouts

This beach is beautiful and has stunning views. It's a black sand beach and the water is transparent as it looks in the photos. The parking might be difficult to find especially during the weekend. The place is a heaven for surfers and people who just want to have a nice picnic on the beach with the family. Overall, a nice get away and has no fee to enter.

Beautiful beach. There's a designated area safe to swim. Just be careful because of the big tides or waves. The beach is very clean with a fine black sand. There's a nice restaurant and ice cream shop around the area. Nice beach to bring family and have a picnic.

Phia Beach – A Hidden Gem of Pure Magic There’s a little part of me that doesn’t want to write this review – Phia Beach feels like a secret, a place so magical it almost deserves to be hidden away. But then again, beauty like this deserves to be shared, even if just a little. The black sand, the turquoise blue waters – it’s like stepping into a dream. The air feels different here, lighter somehow, and the quiet is a balm for the soul. It’s hard to put into words, but there are still places on this earth that feel more beautiful than any description can capture. Phia Beach is one of those. I hear there are penguins that call this place home, though we weren’t lucky enough to spot one during our visit. But that only adds to the allure – there’s magic here, and you just know it’s waiting for the right moment to reveal itself. I’ll forever feel blessed to have experienced this special spot. It’s a true gift, a place that stays with you long after you leave. What a joy it was to witness its quiet beauty.
Stunning southern coastline, Piha Beach is worth the visit. Take a long walk up the beach and find the little hidden cove. Breathtaking. Stop in a Murray’s for a delicious quick bite!

Piha Beach was like one of the paradise of NZ! It was an awesome experience to be here for the 2nd time. The ambiance and the view was memorable. Make sure to bring your favorite camera for taking photos.
Definitely a wild coast. Magnificent beach. Some wonderful walks. Highly recommended.
It's pretty amazing! Simply one of the best spots to visit in the West side of Auckland, without a doubt I should repeat it on summer time!
Awesome beach and love the dark sand!
This place is where I want to retire someday. Easily the most beautiful place I have seen ever. Piha you will always have my heart.
Beautiful nature
Beautiful rock at Piha Beach
Absolutely lovely, friendly community gallery with gorgeous art inside. With a range of priced items for everyone's budget 😍

Awesome little gallery in Piha, showcasing the work of local artists from the Waitakere Ranges. Paintings, ceramics, sculpture, jewellery and more. If you come to Piha you can’t miss a stroll on the beach, a coffee at the local shops and a visit to the gallery! You won’t be disappointed.

If it weren't for my guide ( Louis @ Barefoot tours) I would've missed this place. Thankfully they were open and I found exactly what I had hoped to find as souvenirs of my time in Piha. Local artists here are very talented. Beautiful handcrafted jade, ceramics, books, and prints. One of my favorite stops in all of greater Aukland.

Beautiful art works, with exhibitions from featured local artists plus a good selection of gifts to buy at reasonable prices. Painting, jewellery, ceramics, sculpture, photography and prints all in one very creative space. Well worth a visit
Really eclectic range, amazing big pieces of sculptue and paintings, but also an easily affordable range too, including jewellery. Great gift ideas for people who like the unique and locally-made.

Beautiful and we'll worth the trek! BUT...this is NOT an easy walk. Many, many steps, crossing over rocks on the river, walking along slippery rocks on the cliff face, and generally a difficult walk half the way. Recommend hiking boots, light clothing, and plenty of water. There are toilets at the entrance and places to have a picnic. Great day out.
Great walking track. There was more stairs and steeper than I expected. The view from the bottom of the waterfall is better, but the track is not as well maintained at the one going to the top.

Well maintained path. Flat and easy until you get to the stairs to the waterfall. Beware: small stream crossing, but if it's been raining prepare to get wet! Can swim in the waterfall pool. Worth a dip

The trail to the waterfall is well-maintained, making it accessible for people of all fitness levels. Once you reach the falls area (20mins walk), the view is breathtaking, with water splashing down in a powerful display. We visited around 6:30 pm (March), and the sunlight hitting the falls made the photos absolutely stunning. Highly recommend timing your visit for the golden hour to capture the beauty in its full glory!

Beautiful walk through the “rainforest”. A very short river crossing on stepping-stone natural rocks. A long continuous uphill staircase (over 100 steps). Magnificent waterfall and pool to swim in (in warmer weather).
Very nice hiking track! There are so many different plants. It’s really amazing waterfalls. Most of the time you walk beside a stream.

Lovely walk (though steep at times) through the bush, where you can find ALL the typical flora and fauna of Auckland's bush. The pool at the waterfall is great to cool down (literally) in summer. Pitty the track on the South side of the valley is closed due to the huge slip (you can see it on your way up). The road that takes to the entrance of the track is still restricted to residents, but it is an easy 1k walk from the Piha fire station.

A scenic track leading down to the falls themselves. From the start with a large tree trunk that you can step inside to walking an undulating path with the sounds of the water flowing getting louder as you get closer. A 25 minute walk which is easily doubled as you stop to admire the scenery and the sounds of the birds. Your first site of the falls is through the Bush foliage and then a short few steps and your standing beneath an awesome fall dropping into a pool which is dimmable. You can cross the falls walk up the opposite side and that takes you to the top. You can venture close to the edge but have good boots as it can be slippery. From here you can see the magnificence of the forest spread out before you. There are small look out posts well signed off tracks and plenty to explore.
A gorgeous track in the forest. Access to the falls was closed, but we enjoyed the open section. We were excited to see our first Kereru near the entrance!
Very nice hiking track! There are so many different plants. Most of the time you walk besides a stream. The waterfall was huge because of the amount of rain in the last few days.
Great little beach for paddle boarding and swimming. There is a nearby park and little takeaway shop

French Bay is a very quiet and lovely beach in Auckland. My husband and I went there on 19/10/2023. We had a relaxing stroll there and enjoyed the magnificent views near French Bay Yacht Club. We highly recommend you to visit there if you live near there or drive past there for a walk.

Come here multiple times a week, lovley swimming spot , a few swings and a boat ramps to jump o aswel. climbing trees provide great shelter and great fishing spots here too. Me and my friends always go around the corners and walk around the bays. To the right side of the boat ramp and boat areas is a few steps and at mid-high tide is a lovely swimming spot and very clear water. A few small fish somedays and seaweed can come onto shore alot but all together a wonderful beach with safe people and nice area!
This is one of the best beaches close to Titirangi village. Plenty of car parks, can sit in car and enjoy the beautiful view. Nice sand and people sunbathe etc.
Calm water, not too crowded. Beautiful drive
Belladonna,Archibald, and Mika had an absolute blast, what a fabulous place, we must come again while I'm visiting, 3 worn out lovable labs..
I loved it! Great to see where Colin McCahon lived and painted. And I got a nice little tour!
Interesting place but made fascinating by the volunteer guide who showed us around and gave detail and life to the small cottage. Great to see where he lived and worked.

Absolute must to visit - guided tour by knowledgeable and enthusiastic guide fills in the blanks concerning early history of Colin McCahon - painter extraordinaire. Beautiful setting deep in the bush.
A real treasure to Auckland city. Great even during the rain to sit and think of life when McCahon was living here.
Great slice of Auckland/kiwi history. Would have been an amazing place to work and live, peaceful, inspiring....

I am grateful to be able to enjoy the tranquility of walking and the beauty of the countryside, with birds, trees, and the sea amidst the lush green landscapes near Auckland. Unfortunately, there's dumpted rubbish that seems to be neglected.
Open, quiet and scenic. Only downside is can get smelly if the wind direction isn’t in your favour as sewage ponds are around
The scenery is beautiful.
Great place to walk or bird watch. We used as a place to chill on way to airport!
Winter is not a good time as there are so many insects.
If you plan on coming here make sure you drive - although the walk does consist of many birds there are too many construction trucks driving in and out to make it enjoyable.
A bit overcast here today, but nice ride out on Island Road & track from carpark, haven't been out to this Island in years, Winstone use to have a quarry here. Saturday 3 September 2022.

Left from public car park takes about 30min to walk to very edge and right of the carpark about 15 min to very edge. Can only access a small portion of the island as rest of it is private land and a waste processing factory. Views pretty good, smells a bit iffy but super quiet and feels sorta special.
Not much to see or enjoy. The track is use by cyclists aswell. Dont expect much and you wont be disappointed!
Great ride to the Island from Ambury Farm, around the Bird Sanctuary. This view is looking to the Manukau Heads.

Great weekend walk. Track is well kept making it easy for all ages to walk here. One can easily spend several hours or less than 30mins on the various tracks. Parking is easily available, there is a specfic dog park located off Creamery Rd. This is place is great to see all kinds of birds, take your camera along if your into photography. The only negative point to be noted is the smell you can get from time to time, this depends on the wind direction and for the most part is not too bad but its something to be-aware off.

I come here for the bike trails. Pretty easy, good for beginners. Was a shame one of the carparks were trashed last time I came here with my son (broken beer bottles, rubbish, vomit). Send those animals back to the ZOO!
Awesome views, lots of wildlife namely birds. Sometimes smell can be overwhelming that's why no 5 stars. However, definetily worth a visit, I am regular there over the weekend.
Really great scenic tranquil place, Lots of bird life, black swans
Nice to be out in nature. Nice views. Sometimes there are smells from waste treatment plant but they soon vanish as you walk away

Easy trail with no slope at all. The ocean view was okay. You can see bird sanctuary and farm animals. The birds are black swans and ducks. There are a lot rubbish along the road to Puketutu island which is a big shame! I haven’t never seen so many rubbish in New Zealand at all! Looks like a third world country!

My first track in 2021. This one is very easy to walk, especially for hiking beginners to start with. 20 minutes away from the city downtown in South. Basically it's walking surrounded the Wayercare waste water facility. No impressive view though. Due to some ongoing projects original tracks were blocked we had to take alternative paths. Normally it takes 1.5 hours to complete. Today we took more than two hours to make it. Unfortunately the weather wasn't there for us, otherwise I would make it a 5 stars experience.

Great spot for a walk or a cycle, you can go on longer walks which are about 2 hours or shorter tracks which are around 35 minutes. Paths are a mixture of gravel and tar. No real hills so easy pace. Great for all fitness levels.
Love this! Very long walk but mostly flat. Must check out Albany farm for a free experience petting the many animals

Great place to experience the treated wastewater. The pump station is nearby which pumps treated wastewater into the harbour. Black swans on the water which means mangere treatment plant has done a great job.
Another great place to visit in Auckland. The park as well as the farm animals are a great treat to watch. Well maintained and a place where you can take your family and kids for a day experience.
A wonderful oasis this side of Auckland. Well marked tracks. Great bird hide. Nice and safe and tidy.
Very nice

Excellent Tour! I visited North and South New Zealand with my wife, in the month of Feb 2024 and I must say it was a memorable tour. They exceeded my expectations. They not only took care of every detail of our itinerary but also ensured our stay at the selected hotels was perfect. Each accommodation was handpicked for its comfort, elegance, and prime location. They were very supportive. From the moment we booked, they were there to answer our questions and make sure everything was going smoothly. Highly recommend TT Tour's service!

I had the privilege of joining my son’s school trip as a parent helper to the Māngere Education Centre, and it was truly one of the most enlightening experiences. Although I grew up in Māngere and have walked up the mountain many times in my childhood, I never knew the rich history behind it. Māori history—especially the stories connected to Māngere Mountain—was never taught during my time at school, and I hadn’t realised just how much impact humans have had on the maunga over time. The visit was incredibly informative and thoughtfully delivered. Our guides—Kimiora, Wayne, and Awatea—were knowledgeable, professional, very down-to-earth and deeply engaging. They brought the history of the maunga to life, sharing stories about pre-colonial life, the kūmara pits, pā sites, Māori ways of living, tikanga, and so much more! We had a blast learning the game with the rakau and planting kūmara. One day did not feel like enough time to take it all in😅 Fa’afetai tele lava to the team at Māngere Education Centre for the important mahi you do and for so generously sharing your knowledge with us. Keep on keeping on!

My students and I visited for a guided hikoi around the maunga, Heather was so engaging with her kōrero on its history and geology. She was very patient with my students questions, and we all learned a lot together. I can't wait to return again, highly recommended for school groups.

Wonderful education centre where friendly educators teach children about Mangere Mountain, volcanoes, and Māori culture. Activities for kids are available: we made an erupting volcano, painted another volcano, made mini-poi, did a treasure hunt, and participated in story time. Highly recommended for a hands-on and friendly time without the hustle and bustle of more touristy locations. The educators do the best possible with their limited funding, and their care for childrens education shows!

Went as a parent on a school trip. The talks from the educators were excellent, fun and informative, and really made the trip. Maori History and the history of the volcano, talks about traditional medicine. Thanks for an excellent day.
Leilani & Marcia were awesome!! Thank you for sharing our Maunga's history. Our kids had so much fun. Especially getting dirty while picking the Kumara🙌
Great venue for private functions. Our band (The Repeats) played here for a wedding anniversary recently and the hall looked stunning. Also the accoustics are perfect for a live band.
Had our grad here and nice historical clean venue

Held my son's birthday party here. It's a decent hall for gatherings less than 50 people. It's a bit old, but served our purpose well. It was affordable as well. 36/h for non-peak hours and 45 during peak hours(6pm - 8pm)
Beautiful hall… great for a party or gathering of nearly 50 people.

Great for musical events, birthdays, meetings all the above! You'll be amazed by the old character of this space. The ceiling decor is really something to look at. I would highly recommend this venue if you're looking to host any functions :)
A great place, but come early like before 9am .... Fruits, veggies are really cheap but check and compare prices as they are surprisingly different from stall to stall !

It is still the best marketplace for me after 1 year of going here every Saturday. Lots of fresh veggies and fruits. Mobile phone accessories , clothes, and car accessories. Yummy and tasty food with lots of options. Also got cooking utensils. Lots of parking available though might have to wait if you planning to go after 10am. Opens from morning till 1pm. Recommend to take your shopping bag. Most sellers have card options, but I always prefer taking cash.

Great to wander around having a look at all the crafts, clothing and nic nacs. A little bit of everything. Yummy kai of all cultures. And great veggies to choose from. Parking is really busy so definitely need to be a little patient when looking for a park but slow and steady gets you one. You can even have a look through the Otara shops if to the side. Everything is reasonably priced if you shop around.

Great variety of food, fresh produce and miscellaneous items for sale. We were here at 10 and the place was packed with both people and vehicles, so do come early to get a parking spot. Some stalls sell out early so it pays to visit early. Will definitely come back for the food, especially for the otai!
Lots of choices for vegetables and fruits with cheaper price too. For food section, need more vegetarian options and halal. Overall is good
Went for a walk, May 21, 2025, peaceful, spacious, good pathways, skate park, playground, place to sit in the shade, public toilets, plenty of parking, and a pond.

Great family friendly park for walks, activities and sports. Skate park and activity centre available on site with ample parking and local shops and restaurants nearby. Walking distance from Ormiston mall, hospital and movies. Clean facilities perfect for general use and low-scale events.

This is a really nice park to walk, cycle or generally hang out in. There are ponds, tracks and a playground for the kids. And a lot of space to explore. It's far enough from the main shopping areas to be quiet, but not enough to be isolated.

Very big park and lots of space to walk. There are path created for walking. Lots of rugby players practice here. There are good parking spaces around the park. This park can be improved by installing some chairs and shelters in different places for walkers to rest.
Great place to entertain the kids great for all the family to exercise via the walking tracks. Also beautiful sunsets to view here.

My favourite walking location. Many different routes. Breathtaking views from some of the elevated spots. Quiet and not many other members of the public. A bit of a secret gem. Walking tracks are medium to hard. The bottom of the reserve to the top is approximately 100 meters of elevation. Many entrance points including the top and the bottom car parking spots.
Nice quiet spot with kind hearted locals and friendly dogs, amazing views at sunset but bring a torch if you think you'll stay late.
Nice place for a walk. Nice views of the sunset.
Its killer of a hill up to the reservoir but a good training route.
Short uphill walk. I always come here just to get some fresh air and some quiet time...
Stunning views for sunrise and sunset Perfect spot to catch both There is a sitting area if u wanna have a little picnic Also its dog friendly.

Come here with my partner from time to time. The walk is great and really accessible. The view is great and you can see everything in east Auckland. Recommend going on the bush walk and hanging out looking over the skyline.

My husband and I went hiking at Point View Summit today, 28/1/2024. The views at the Summit are incredible and amazing. We walked for around 5 minutes from the parking area to the Summit which is ideal for anyone who wants to enjoy the panoramic up there. The Summit is very tranquil so we can enjoy the peaceful moments on Sunday. We highly recommend you to get to the Summit and enjoy the magnificent views.
Used to be a great view but now most trees grow taller ! Blocked the view partially 😅
Breathe taking views, reaching the top is so worth it, there is also a 7000 step return track route going to the bottom of the reserve, picnic spots and open field area halfway to fly some kites❤️👍👌

The Laird Thomson track to Te Waha point lookout from north of piha car park is closed due to a slip taking out part of the track at the very start of the walk. So I carried on to the Rose track trailhead car park and walked that track as it takes you to Whites beach, but it also links onto the Laird Thomson track to Te Waha point lookout. It's roughly a 30-minute walk from the car park to lookout it's all downhill, so be prepared to walk back up to car park. Spectacular views on a sunny day.

Stunning. Can do a hike from along the beach, up through the rainforest, to this point. There are a few seats along get east. Or else there is another hike down. You get a stunning view across two beaches and then the ocean straight out in front of you. There is also a seat at the lookout where you can watch the world go by or the sun set or rise. Great hidden gem.
Great place for a careful walk. Track has steep drops. However, great views at the top.
Track is well worth the view. Make a point of heading to the trail for whites beach. Do the lookout.
Enjoyable walk for an afternoon. Great views up and down the coast.

I really love this track. You can see breath taking ocean views and bush view at the same time. It’s rather easy. I think the best of all is that the whole track has mobile phone signal, which means you can listen to your favourite tunes when you do the hiking!

Beautiful track with amazing views, well kept track and enjoyed our walk up. We went up at the perfect time when no one was around, met a few people on the way down but it's not crowded at all. So peaceful up there. Mostly flat but a steady incline to get that heart pumping.

A really nice, clean and almost flat short trail from the parking area to a stream crossing and the start of White Track. It takes about 10 minutes to walk to the end of Marawhara Track. It’s a Bush walk trail with woods, palms, and ferns. Very easy to walk for anyone. At the end of the trail, and the start of White Track, there is a shallow stream crossing and a good swimming hole. Take your swimsuit (togs) and relax in the water. From the crossing, it is about a 45 minute walk to White Beach. If you just continue along White Track uphill from the stream crossing, there are several overlook that have really great views north to Piha Beach and the mountains surrounding Piha.
Steep climb to expansive views over Piha before decent via road and track to Whites Beach. Steep road but rewarding views.
Well maintained track. easy trail

The Laird Thomson track is closed to access Te Waha point lookout from the north of piha Car Park due to a slip taking out part of the track at the very start of the walk. If you want to go to Te Waha point lookout, park at Rose track trailhead, and that track goes to whites Beach and also links onto Laird Thomson track to Te Waha point lookout. You can still go to see the caves near Laird Thomson track.

Nice short walk to Te Waha Point with wonderful view. Roughly 20 mins up, 10 mins back. But it’s truly difficult to find the entrance of the track even if you have a map. The entrance is behind a rock among the cliffs, no sign out there, hardly to see. Go further north along the cliffs, pass those caves you can see, to the corner end behind then you are all good to climb up.😀

Not a bad track. Special features of the track is that you end up going twice over a slow moving stream as it curves up a mountain. Lots of Kauri trees, birds, mushrooms, and rocks that allow for some awesome photo opportunities. Once you get up the top, it starts to flatten out until you reach a inter-junction, in which you can either head towards Glenesk Road (Right) or head further along a ridge towards another track. It's not an easy climb as it was a bit slippery and a few rocks to step over.
great views, only a short climb from end of North Piha
Beautiful views - Gets straight into steps and uphill - seats at the top for a pit stop.
Once you know this track, you will truly know pain.

On Scenic Drive, nestled in the picturesque Waiatarua region of the Waitākeres, Parkinson Lookout is a scenic gem 💎 The lookout offers a breathtaking 😍 panorama (obscured by some trees) of Auckland's lush landscapes, with views stretching across the stunning skyline 🏙 and surrounding hills ⛰️ It is only a short, pretty even walk from the carpark. People can immerse themselves in the tranquility of the area 😌 taking in the fresh air and natural beauty 🌲🌊🐦 making it an ideal location for a moment of reflection or a leisurely picnic on the grassy area. The lookout is particularly famous for being one of the highest elevations in Auckland 😮 and for its gorgeous sunsets 🌅 where the sky transforms into a canvas of vibrant colours, providing a perfect backdrop for photography.

I recently visited the viewpoint and found it to be a mixed experience. The signs leading to the location were not very clear, especially in the evening, making it quite challenging to find the spot. However, once you arrive, the view is definitely worth it. I recommend visiting around sunset, as this timing allows you to enjoy both the breathtaking evening colors and a full view of the city. With some improvements in signage, this could be a fantastic destination!
Lovely views of Auckland and the North Shore from the top of the Waitakere Ranges The lookout point could benefit from some trimming of nearby bush and treetops.

6/10. Needing a bit of maintenance so that people can continue to not have to use the more dangerous unofficial lookouts to get a good gander of Tamaki from the Waitakeres. The wee carpark also needs urgent attention as there is serious erosion happening - I think due in part to waterflow below the gravel - causing deep, crevices to appear making it unusable on one side to any lower vehicles.
Parking limited Good view of the CBD and surrounding suburbs
What a beautiful place. So quiet on a Sunday morning, we were the only ones there. Stunning views over auckland and being spring, the flowers are coming out in bloom. Well worth a visit.
First time there. Interesting history. Yes, amazing site and views. 4/5 stars as was keen to see the inside of the original house. Like time travel.
Went here earlier on a weekday and I didn't see anyone except a cyclist. Beautiful views and nice and quiet
What an amazing view out over the city. The grounds/carpark are open now. If your going to piha, this is well worth the short 5 min detour.
Beautiful view and lovely quiet spot to go to. Great bit of history and an amazing lady who has lived an inspiration life. RESPECT 🤙

Beautiful Park! Great hiking gorgeous trails and views. The trails are well marked and easy to follow. Some elevation but extremely doable. The staff at the visitor center was very helpful and well informed. She gave us excellent advice and information for a great hike and shortcut back to town.

Went for a short visit. Lookouts was awesome. The staff and guide were extremely helpful. Driving to this place was fun, the roads were quite narrow, might want to avoid taking big busses to this place. Drive to this place was short. Parking was easy to find. Looking forward to trying out the trails soon.

I have been to this visitor center efore. It is very nicely taken care of with plenty of parking and easy access. The view from up there is fantastic and the near by nature trail is beautiful. I recommend checking it out but be careful of the drive there. The roads are tight if you are not used to driving NZ roads.

Such beautiful and relaxing hiking trails here! The centre is well setup so you get to have a short tour before your walk and a good rest after. The view is magnificent! Most important it is not far, with multiple choices of the walking trails fit for all ages.

Beautiful place and nice trails. We did the nature trail one (the entrance near the car park) which is a short walk with some stairs in the lower trail. if you don't want to do stairs just do the upper loop. It have another long trail start near the center. The center is great for the kids they are super happy! you can buy some suovenir postcard and coffee here. Oh! try the ice-cream after done yoir trail, it was amazing! love this place!
Awesome track flat for 30mins then heavy slippery downwards passed a beautiful huge Kauri. 1 hour either way
Track is closed due to kauri dieback. Still a cool little walk that you can do, the current walk is about 15 minutes one way. Pretty cool for photos because of the tracks leading lines.
This place is closed by Auckland council due to some desease in this area... something called Kauri dieback desease... dont waste ur time n petrol to drive there...

Nice trail for a weekend outing with 3 tracks from 1 hour to 2.5 hours. Mostly through thick woods and with some beautiful glimpses of the seas and the beaches. Complete with a visitor centre and a small cafe. Very popular over the weekend with families and pets coming from the city.

The Beveridge, Pipeline and Slip tracks make for a great hike to go on with friends. The route is easy to follow, although there are a few steep inclines and the gravel road can require some careful navigation at times. There is a lot to enjoy, including beautiful native plants and birds and amazing views of the dam below. The visitor centre also has lookouts where you can appreciate the size of the valley, mountains, and dam and watch kereru flying. There is plenty of parking near the visitor centre.

A 6.1km loop trail last weekend with my family, it was really a good trail.. It has a well formed track, 210m elevation and considered moderately challenging route and a beautiful view of the reservoir. It was drizzling but great experience.

Did the whole loop around took me and mum and my aunty 3hrs for the whole thing🤣was a good walk though difficulty 3/5. Recommend not to bring young children aged 1-6 as there are steep hills and not recommended for elderly. Other than that great walk out yesterday

Completed the Arataki Beveridge Track loop. It was just okay, nothing special to be honest. There's an option to do just Beveridge track too which is what I'd recommend. Entrance to that is on your left when entering Visitor Centre car park.
Spectacular
good feel
A must to go to recommended for people all ages 10 minute walk through the bushes and to the road going back to the car park dogs allowed on leash
What a spot! Stunning view
Found this little gem hidden away in Titirangi. Easy walk up and can also drive to the top if you prefer. Loved the view over Auckland!
Great views, even has a small carpark 😊
Great outlook, it's worth it when you're in Titirangi. 😘
Great ambience good food excellent service
Awesome community

We took the grandchildren here (7 and 5) at their request. The art and the building are phenomenal. The grandchildren liked the stairs, the elevators and the learning area the best, but we spent a very happy hour there!

Te Uru Waitākere Contemporary Gallery is an absolute gem! This is the place to come to if you want to experience new and contemporary art. They change their exhibits and installations often, to make every visit fresh and interesting. Your personal taste will inform the visit. Some contemporary installation are brilliantly inspired and inspiring, and showcases local New Zealand history and artists. Although I could appreciate the passion and effort that went into creating those works of art, I just didn't "get" some of the pieces. The building itself is an architectural marvel. It also offers beautiful outside views, displaying the wooded areas and the harbour as art itself. Well worth a visit!

I am in love! This gallery is spacious, 5 leveled and filled with stunning, engaging art. There is even a rooftop terrace to take beautiful, scenic photos and take a moment to admire the nature around you.

I love this gallery. I always visit when I travel up from south island to see my family. The water colour paintings by Gretchen Albrecht at Dec/Jan xmas holidays were a colour feast for the eyes. Really enjoyable. The views from the different levels building are a real treat too. The portage Ceramics award pieces here are always special to see. This place is a gem. Its gallery store is nice too.

Te Uru is a wonderful contemporary art gallery. Highest recommendation. This is the place to come to in order to experience exciting new art. The building is a brilliant example of Judy Stout and David Mitchell's architecture. Here's some close up photos of the architecture's careful detailing. Wonderful staff.
My parents 'owned' this tree from 1956 on 12 French Bay rd. Later called Otitori Bay.. The tourist bus would stop for a photo shoot.
I've been here on a few occasions during the past year, and there's nothing
Beautiful
Train
good

Had a look around today , gardens in autumn shades. Got be worth going back in the for the camellias and other flowering shrubs. A little disappointed about the lack of butterflies today, but that I guess there will be more in the spring. Aside from that the walk ways are reasonably accessible , some stairs in some parts. Still well worth a look at this hidden gem.
Absolutely lovely to wander around. Calming and natural. Also great to see locals making use of the facilities. The monarch butterflies and caterpillars were a treat to see!

Only $5 entry to these beautiful sprawling gardens. Plenty of picnic spots and seats, and trees that provide shade on hot days. The monarch butterfly house is lovely too. Great place to take the family for a relaxing time.

Delightful, peaceful wooded garden with lots of lovely clearings with seats to sit on. Also there are a number of cute Summer Houses dotted around the garden. The Butterfly House has several lovely Monarchs in it. They even thought of an umbrella over the fish pond to keep the water cooler for the Goldfish. Parking is in the grounds. A wonderful project run by volunteers - thank you so much!

The reality turned out to be worse than I expected. The garden looks like a regular track. In the butterfly pavilion, there were three butterflies and five larvae. I expected to see something similar to the butterfly pavilion at the Singapore airport and organized flower beds or well-kept meadows with benches. Here, even the benches were dirty. Why is there an entrance fee for this?
Nice quaint beach which has a hiking trail too, but there is no sandy beach. It is a marshy beach where locals come to fish. It is a nice spot to relax within the city.

Quite little beach, lovely for picnics and it has a nice easy walking track to Blockhouse Bay Beach. The ocean is not suitable for swimming which is a shame because the water looks inviting. When the tide is out you can walk around the rocks but need to be mindful of quick sand. No car access to the beach front, so you have to carry everything down and back up a steep hill. Plenty of road parking at the top, try to make 1 trip with everything to avoid walking up the hill continuously. Read the Green Bay Beach signs as it gives you important information you must know.

On 24/9/2023, my husband and I went to Green Bay Beach for a walk. Unfortunately, the weather was not so good and it rained for most of the day. We managed to take a stroll along the beach. There was a steep trail leading to the beach and we took our steps carefully as the floor was very slippery. There were some people walking their dogs, fishing and walking there. The beach was quite quiet so we could enjoy the tranquility and peacefulness there. We recommend you to wear your gumboots there as the beach is muddy and slippery.
It was fine, but I didn't find much happening.

Wear shoes or gumboots! Rocky, muddy, crabs and glass. Not good for swimming or fishing as is polluted. Apart from all of that, the scenery is nice, cute little rock pools and crabs, not many people. Also has a picnic table and a nice seat to sit on to look at the view and has stairs leading up to a walk up along the cliff.

I will remember this church forever in my memory. Where I shared the day with the rest of my siblings a wonderful service for our beloved departed brother. What an amazing venue. It felt like one belongs there when you are in there. My first time in it's domain and besides the funeral service it felt just right. The priest was on point delivering a wonderful service. Amen. 🙏

Quiet, tranquil and a holy place to be with God. The Parish Priest now Fr. Sam is very welcoming. The Church is also blessed a hall and a very generous parking. The school - Monte Cecilia is just beside it where its ground is also utilised for Church activities such Holy Week celebration, Christmas and other big activities. Has vigil mass and two masses on Sunday 9am and 530pm.

Great welcoming church. Father Sam is awesome. Professional & caring yet entertaining with a great sense of humor. Plus there's morning tea after mass Sunday mornings to give the kids (and adults) something to look forward to.
Excellent delivery of the message of god by father Sam. He is a good and humble priest.
Filipino Priest is the best! Reason why we kept coming back here as the vibe is so friendly. Church is clean and there is a children’s room.
Belfast is looking a bit sad atm the track is close temperely, looking forward to seeing it in the future

. (12/2017) This reserve is renamed as Belfast Reserve. On walking around, it feels like an ignored and abandoned reserve. Not maintained very well. There are seats for taking rest and enjoying the views but you cannot sit because of algae all over them. There are walkways which are mostly covered by tree leaves and you have to be careful while walking over them. Broken trees and extended bushes block your way at places. There are stairways but you have to exercise caution due to gravel over them. You may run across few smelly corners and have to avoid wasps flying all around. Could not notice any public restroom at this location which is a pity provided this reserve serves as merging point for multiple walkways. There are three different walkways, one towards Belfast Street, other towards Hillsborough Cemetery and last one towards Hillsborough Bay. At least one of the walkways has a happy ending. Hillsborough Bay walkway ends towards beautiful Taylors Bay with beautiful beach and well maintained seating etc. No dedicated parking area available for this big reserve although ample street parking can be found at all entrances. The main entrance from Hillsborough Bay has nice seating spaces and well maintained walking area. There is wheelchair accessible entrance but tracks are definitely not wheelchair friendly.
Great little reserve to get into some fairly decent cardio packed into a tight little spot Hard to know that is inside NZ's biggest city as well.
Lovely fresh walk in nature give you a brain boost and generate new neutrons. May be!
Great place to let the kids loose while you sit and watch the water.

Freedom camping spot near the airport. It's got toilets, a water fountain, and space for larger campervans. Plus there's a nice walking path along the water. It's a great spot if you're coming from or headed to the airport and need a place to stay for the night.

Excellent reserve with plenty of green space, parking and clean facilities . Fairy Falls in Auckland is an absolute gem, offering a breathtaking immersion in nature. The scenery is truly magnificent, with a stunning backdrop of mountains, lush forest trees, and panoramic views that stretch to the city and the iconic Sky Tower. The highlight, of course, is the waterfall itself, a cascade of clear water that truly lives up to its name, resembling a graceful, white fairy as it plunges down. It's a unique and unforgettable experience. I wholeheartedly recommend Fairy Falls to anyone seeking a peaceful escape into nature, especially those who appreciate the beauty of waterfalls. The best time to visit is during the summer or spring, when you can even take a refreshing swim in the pool at the base of the falls. A practical tip: be sure to eat a full meal before you go. The walk to the falls is a bit of a trek, and the return journey, particularly the uphill sections, can be moderately challenging. Having a good meal beforehand will give you the energy you need. You'll find convenient amenities like bathrooms at the start of the trail and ample car parking. Fairy Falls is perfect for a variety of activities: hiking, walking, running with your dog, capturing stunning photos, and simply soaking in the beautiful views. It's a fantastic place to create lasting memories and connect with nature.

Please be aware that there are lots and lots of dog lovers with their dogs there so if you are scared of dogs, you should be careful about hiking there. A Volcanic Playground Loved by Locals and Dogs Alike! If you’re searching for a nearby escape with amazing views and loads of space, look no further than Big Kin Reserve (Big King). It's a volcanic maunga – part of Auckland’s ancestral mountains – with a well-maintained circular path that takes around 30–35 minutes to complete The off‑leash dog area is a real highlight. There are wide flat sections for pups to chase balls, snuffle, and socialize, plus more rugged, hilly bits to keep walks interesting Most evenings you’ll find a friendly crowd of dog‑owners catching up while their dogs burn off energy—be prepared to make furry friends! Climb to the summit and you’re treated to sweeping panoramas across Mt Eden, the Waitākere Ranges, and beyond The summit even has a bench so you can pause and soak it all in. Paths are mostly sealed and pushchair‑friendly at first, though there are some steps closer to the top—just enough to keep it fun for all fitness levels . Whether you’re after a quick workout, a leisurely family walk, or prime dog‑off‑leash area, Big Kin Reserve has it all—and the community vibe makes it feel extra special. Highly recommended for locals and visitors alike

This historic landmark is on top of One Tree Hill in Cornwall Park, and the platform area around the obelisk provides an excellent viewpoint for panoramic views of the Auckland area. One Tree Hill is a 182-metre (597 ft) volcanic peak formed by scoria cones from 3 volcanic craters. It is an important memorial place for both Māori and other New Zealanders On the summit of the hill is an obelisk, a memorial to Māori. Before the obelisk stands a bronze statue of a Māori warrior. The stone obelisk was designed by Richard Atkinson Abbot and completed in 1940, but the unveiling of the obelisk was delayed until after World War II on 24 April 1948. This was in keeping with Māori custom of not holding such ceremonies during a time of bloodshed. Beneath it is the grave of Sir John Logan Campbell who bequeathed £5,000 for the obelisk. His grave is a plain granite slab, ornamented only by a bronze wreath. It lies in the middle of the viewing platform, on axis with the main memorial plaques on the Obelisk base. Unfortunately, the trees that the hill was famous for (that are visible in some older photos) are now gone. They were all destroyed in protests by the Maori people to the injustices forced upon them by the government. It is a popular place for locals to walk, bike, or run, and also a popular place for tourists staying in the Auckland area to visit to enjoy the views and get some great photos. The trains are well-maintained, and the tracks wind through charming scenery, making each ride exciting. What truly makes this place special is the dedicated team of volunteers who run it. Their passion and hard work create a welcoming, joyful atmosphere for visitors. They operate the trains with such care and enthusiasm, ensuring every child and adult! leaves with a smile. It’s heartwarming to see a community-driven attraction that brings so much happiness to families. A few tips for visitors: - Bring plenty of $2 coins（or change) for multiple rides—kids will definitely want to go more than once! - Arrive early, as it can get busy. - Pack a picnic—there’s space to relax while kids watch the trains go by. - Don’t forget sunscreen and hats on sunny days, as shade is limited. This place runs on passion, not profit, so supporting it helps keep the magic alive. We’re so grateful for the volunteers who make these memories possible. If you’re looking for a simple, wholesome, and budget-friendly outing, Waipuna Miniature Trains is a must-visit! Highly recommended for families with young children.🚂💛

Who with: Two medium-sized dogs If you’re looking for a local dog walk in the Mt Wellington / Panmure area, Mt Wellington Domain is a great option with open grassy spaces, well-kept tracks, and a peaceful vibe. It’s not as crowded as some of the bigger parks, which makes it ideal if you’ve got reactive dogs or just want a quieter walk. There’s a loop track that’s mostly flat with a gentle incline, perfect for getting the dogs’ energy out without needing to hike. The paths are a mix of gravel and grass, and even after rain it wasn’t too muddy. My two dogs had a good trot and there was plenty of room to keep distance from others where needed. TIP: No off-leash area here, so bring a long lead if you want your dogs to roam a bit more — but keep them under control. Also no bins along the track, so you’ll need to take your poop bags home or back to the carpark. Easy parking at the entrance off Mountain Road, and the main loop starts right from there. No toilets or water fountains that I saw, so bring what you need. Would I recommend it? Yes — it’s a good, low-key spot for local dog walking without the crowds, especially if you’re in Mt Wellington or nearby suburbs.

And it can be chilly even when it's sunny down below, so bring a jacket or something. Oh, and pack some water, because you'll work up a thirst on the way up. Another thing – the car park is tiny. Like, maybe 8-10 cars max. If you go on a weekend, get there early or you might miss out. And speaking of missing out, don't even think about going if it looks like rain. There's absolutely nowhere to shelter, you don't want to be trekking back down that hill in a downpour. One last thing: that volcanic crater is seriously steep. If you've got little ones or anyone who's a bit wobbly on their feet, you'll want to keep a close eye on them. If you're up for a mini-adventure with a killer view, Mount Wellington is the place to be.

We had a wonderful family adventure, walking out to Motukaraka Island yesterday. We initially tried to access it from Motukaraka Reserve on Puriri St, but discovered that the track from there is *closed*, possibly permanently. (The stairs down to the beach have been removed from the lower half of the cliff). We then attempted to access the island along the beach from Beachlands Wharf (there are carparks, toilets and a playground there). We found this quite successful as an adventure at low tide for a family of adults and teens, but I would issue caution for families with very young children because there were a couple of points at which we had an awkward clambour up/down rocks at the base of the cliff and the beach can be muddy and slippery in places. However, saying that, there was a family group with fairly young children (and a dog) that came over after us and somehow managed. The access to the island, even heading into low tide was muddy and wet (slippery in places). If you don't like getting your feet wet, definitely *bring/wear a pair of gumboots*. Be very aware of the tide times while you are there. We left Beachlands Wharf about 1.5 hours before low tide and were able to circumnavigate the island and get back to the wharf by 30 mins after low tide. The cliffs are beautiful, and there are some small caves on the seaward side of the island. There is a single access point to the island's plateau: a set of steps beside the Motukaraka Island sign. These steps are fairly solid, but become increasingly overgrown with Cutty Grass as you get higher and the view from the top is almost completely non-existant, obscured by vegetation. We didn't persist beyond the fork in the faint track at the top, but we did see a couple Karaka plants with orange fruit (Note: the seeds are very toxic). All in all, a perfect adventure for our teenage family. We would do it again!

I first saw the Town Hall when I arrived in Auckland, and later I had the chance to see it more closely during my time in the city. The building already stands out from the outside, with its classic architecture that contrasts with all the modern things around it. But the most beautiful part is definitely inside. The main hall, used for concerts, is a stunning space. It looks like something from a movie, and it has a huge, historic organ that is still preserved. It’s one of those instruments that impress you just by looking at it. I loved that many original details are still there: the tiles, the stained glass windows, the stair railings, the wooden floors — all well preserved and in good condition. You can tell they really care about the history of the place. It’s a building with a strong presence in the city, a local landmark and the site of historic events, like the visit of The Beatles in 1964 and even The Rolling Stones in 1965. It’s worth going in if you’re in the city center, even just for a short visit. It’s not always open to the public, but there are often events and concerts. I recommend it. It’s a piece of Auckland’s history.

Auckland War Memorial Museum – A Must-Visit Historical Gem Visiting the Auckland War Memorial Museum was truly an enriching and unforgettable experience. It offers a fascinating journey through New Zealand's history, including its cultural heritage, involvement in global conflicts, and connections with other nations. The museum is filled with powerful photographs, engaging videos, and thoughtfully curated exhibits that truly bring the past to life. The infrastructure is impressive—majestic high ceilings, open and spacious interiors, and a calming, respectful atmosphere throughout. It's a three-story building with plenty to explore, and visitors are provided with a map to help navigate each level with ease. There’s also a lot of parking available outside, and the views around the museum are simply beautiful. Inside, you’ll also find a library for those who want to dive even deeper into history, a cozy café area to relax and recharge, and some amazing jet models and Greek sculptures on display that add a wonderful visual element to the experience. Whether you're a history enthusiast or simply curious about New Zealand’s past, this museum is an ideal place to spend an entire day. With a minimal entry fee and so much to discover, I would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Auckland who has an interest in history, culture, or architecture.

And let's not forget the military sections which are so well done. I'll have to return when the rest is available for viewing.

The Auckland Baptist Tabernacle is a heritage-listed church located near the corner of Queen Street & Karangahape Road at tge edge of the Auckland Business District in Auckland, New Zealand. It was built Easter Monday 1884, was completed 12 May 1885 at a cost of £14,000 and is one of the oldest buildings in Auckland city. Thomas Spurgeon was the pastor of the church The prominent site at the top of Queen Street was secured at it was Initially intended that the Church would face Karangahape Road but the plans were revised so it was actually constructed with the main façade on Queen Street. This meant the portico was visible from the harbour. Although one of the biggest buildings to be constructed in the city at the time, it took only one year to build from 1884-85. As well as having very good acoustics its auditorium was also the largest room in the city, able to accommodate over 1500 people at the time.

This sculpture was the first large, abstract public artwork to be commissioned in Auckland. Created by Marté Szirmay, who was a graduate student at Elam School of Fine Arts, the sculpture is made up of eight interlocking aluminium pieces. With a seemingly brutalist look and feel, and made from utilitarian materials, Smirnoff Centenary Sculpture was designed to remind passersby of the industrial history of Newmarket. The highly reflective surfaces were also intentional, mirroring the hustle and bustle of the surrounding streets. Using manufactured materials and reflective finishes became a familiar characteristic of the artist’s work.Szirmay won the first Smirnoff Sculpture award, which included the commission to create this sculpture for the Newmarket Borough centenary celebrations. It was installed at the intersection of Khyber Pass and Broadway in October 1969. In 2010, as part of an upgrade of the green space on the corner known as Lumsden Green, the sculpture was moved to its current site, closer to Broadway.

Muriwai is also a great spot for paragliding, horseback riding, and fishing. The area is equipped with picnic facilities, making it a perfect place for a family day out. Whether you're looking to relax on the sand, catch some waves, or explore the natural beauty, Muriwai Beach offers a diverse and memorable experience for all visitors.

It doesn’t quite have the same ring to it as the Yellow Brick Road but the Red Fence is just as colourful and much easier to find. In fact, if you are in downtown Auckland, it’s hard to miss the Red Fence as it stretches out along the waterfront keeping the goings-on at Auckland’s port in and the public out. The decision to paint the wrought iron fence brilliant red was inspired. A fence, after all, is just a fence but with a splash of paint this particular fence became a city landmark worthy of heritage status. Construction of the Red Fence began in 1913 but was halted because of Auckland’s infamous waterfront strike. When the strike collapsed and port operations resumed, the fence began to snake its way along Quay Street. Ornamental gates and lamps were added and a gate keeper was appointed for each of the 12 gates. Sadly, the gate keepers are long gone and most of the gates are padlocked but it is still possible to follow the line of bright red paint along the waterfront and to learn the history of this area. The Red Fence Heritage Walk starts at the Voyager New Zealand Maritime Museum and finishes about an hour later at the Ports of Auckland building sitting next to the helipad at Mechanics Bay. Numbered signs provide information about points of interest along the way making this an easy self-guided walk. After passing the ochre-coloured Ferry Building, Queen’s Wharf (home to Shed 10 and the Cloud), Admiralty Steps and Captain Cook and Marsden wharves, you’ll reach Britomart Point Rock which marks the spot where, in 1840, the British flag was raised in a ceremony marking the foundation of Auckland. Britomart Point was demolished during the 1880s but across the road is its namesake, the Britomart area popular for trendy shopping, good coffee and a Saturday city market. The half- way point of the heritage walk is the Rainbow Warrior memorial which commemorates the sinking of the Greenpeace anti-nuclear protest ship, the Rainbow Warrior, at Marsden wharf in 1985. The Rainbow Warrior was irreparable and she is at rest now in Matauri Bay in the Far North, providing a site for diving and a sanctuary for fish. The ensuing outrage (the French government agents only served 2 years of a 10 year sentence) and public relations disaster (for France) strengthened New Zealand’s anti-nuclear stance and irrevocably changed New Zealand’s foreign and defence policy. The remainder of the heritage walk follows the Red Fence past more wharves, and the banks of containers and sky high cranes of the container terminal. The fence ends finally at the Ports of Auckland building situated next to the heliport at Mechanics Bay. Beyond this point, the road carries on to the eastern bays and unobstructed views across the harbour. This is an out-and-back walk and there is no danger of losing your way. Just follow the Red Wrought Iron Fence

Thanks Mike for such an awesome tour. I’m 100% impressed with Mike’s passion about he’s wine, no short cut or compromises, all the efforts and detailed works they put together to deliver these top of the top wines in Australia and New Zealand! Absolutely recommend to any wine enthusiast!

Smiths Bush is one of the six ancient forests to explore in Auckland. The Auckland urban area was once covered in lush, tall forest. The legacy of this majestic world remains in only a few precious patches around Auckland, many of which are easily accessible and well worth a visit. Kahikatea forests are found in locations with high water tables, such as wet depressions and flat terraces beside major watercourses. These same landforms are perfect for farming and building houses so kahikatea forests have been almost entirely cleared from urban Auckland. One of the best examples left is is Smiths Bush, a green urban oasis of soaring trees and raucous tūī, right beside the northern motorway. Nestled within the kahikatea is a magnificent stand of pūriri. The forest is almost rectangular in shape with very large, mature pūriri trees dominant in the centre. Large taraire, kowhai, titoki, karaka, tawa, matai, miro and tōtara are also present in the canopy. Surrounding the pūriri-dominated forest is a dense stand of kahikatea . Smaller trees and shrubs growing beneath the canopy include mahoe, hangehange, kawakawa and several Coprosma species. Pūriri is an essential tree to Māori, who use it for various purposes. The wood is durable and rugged, making it useful for carving, furniture, and buildings.

Beautiful volcanic island with an easy trail to the top. The one hour hike is rewarded with a fantastic panoramic view of the shoreline - including the Auckland skyline - and surrounding islands. Great day excursion

The last bit has some medium grade steps that did push my cardio a little, but plenty of beautiful places to stop and admire the view (catch your breath). We went at the very end of Spring and the weather was great but not yet too hot. Take plenty of fluids and snacks as there are no shops on the island, and make sure to only take your rubbish home. We went on the 10.15 am ferry, which gave us ample time to do several walks before the last ferry back at 4.30pm. We did a slow stroll to the summit and followed the cave track on the way down. Then we branched off for the Kidney Fern trail (remarkable little plants with leaves so thin you can see through them), and finished with a walk around the coast to see the historic baches. A fabulous day out suitable for most ages and abilities.

Beautiful track! Although the visibility was poor when I visited, the track itself is amazing and the lava caves were fantastic to see! I took the 10.30am ferry, and it took me (relatively young, fit, and healthy) 40 minutes from the wharf to the summit, 15 minutes to walk the loop around the crater, 30 minutes to the lava caves then 20 minutes exploring the lava caves, and 30 minutes back to the wharf leaving me woth half an hour before the 2.20 ferry It was quite physically demanding! And very warm due to the volcanic rock but well worth it!

Very cool to see, information panels on the way offer good insights. We saw a funny little wood hut on the way to the summit and wish we’d know what it was used for. The only toilets on the island are at the wharf, over an hours walk away. It gets very hot midday but the tubes offer a sharp drop in temperature. Bring a torch and some guts if you plan on going in.
