The woman also poured decent amounts of wine in the glasses, compared to other wineries where we had wine tasting. The winery is cute and has a cosy outdoor terrace. The woman serving us the wine was knowledgable and very good at her job!

Visited the vineyard in January 2024 and would recommend others to drop by as well. Knowledgeable staff, excellent wines away from the crowds. A walk away from the main road - easily reachable by car as well.
Spectacular views!! You can see Auckland CBD too

Beautiful lookout with a picnic area, right by EcoZip ziplines, also near a hiking trail to the vineyard poderi Crisci. The trail itself is quite difficult, but Trigg Hill itself is easy access with beautiful views and would be a great place to bring a blanket and some snacks on a warm day. The top of the hill can be a bit windy, but still worth it
Awesome wandering destination point. Really gives you perspective of how big Waiheke island is since it's smack dab in the middle.
Brilliant views and well maintained. Great location for locals and visitors alike
Would be great place to watch the sunset. Nice grass area for a picnic.

A great experience walking around here at night a few days before Christmas. Everyone in this neighbourhood has put a lot of effort into decorating their houses on the outside and creating an attraction for heaps of people. Will definitely be coming here every year!
Stunning - entertaining for young and old
Effin loved it hahah i was impresed
Best in the North West.
You guys rock - thank you for the work and display you all put on.
Magnificent! We arrived at 4 and the welcome was the best we had received in all our New Zealand experiences. The wines are simply delicious, nothing has been added... The 4 Frenchmen

Completely unplanned visit to this great wine producer winery which inspired me to give Chardonnays another go. Great wine tasting hosted by a very friendly and knowledgeable lady. Would highly recommend a visit here for sure and be prepared to stock up on a few wines too.

One of the best family producers in Kumeu. Amazing history, outstanding wines and insightful and informative staff. Their 2022 Estate Barrique fermented Chardonnay is definitely one of the best Chardonnays in the Auckland region. NZWINEPRO - Auckland Wine Tours is a tour company that can take you to this winery and they can also show you through the barrel room and production facility. Highly recommend them both.

We drove straight from the Auckland airport to Kumeu River Winery. It takes around 40 minutes. This is a family owned winery, very welcoming and personal. The lady who conducted the tasting was really friendly, informative, and professional. Unfortunately, the bubbles and premium Chardonnay were not available for tasting, however we did taste two pinot noirs, 1 pinot gris, 1 rosé, and 2 Chardonnays. Cost for a tasting is $10 pp.

Really surprised and impressed to find this gem in Kumeu. My husband and I have been traveling and working at wineries for the last 3 and a half years and we have rarely had such an amazing experience at a cellar door. Their wines are lovely all around, perhaps particularly appealing to our palates. We’re a bit picky with our Pinots but their Hawke’s Bay Pinot Noir was beautiful, full and well balanced. We were also impressed with the price point, I would expect to pay more for hand picked wine made with such care. Thank you Fiona for answering our questions and for the great tasting.

Awesome weekend! Great for the whole family!! Everything is well spread out, with heaps of bins and toliets. Saturday is very busy so best to get there early! friday or sunday is abit more relaxed.. lots of cool cars, caravans, bikes, monster trucks! Kids under 12 free.

It is a great place to enjoy viewing classic cars from across the globe. If you're after car parts for your restoration project or wanting to buy something already done, this is the place. Lots of food and music are appropriate to the theme of the event and very family-friendly activity.
Turned up at about 0900 on Sunday, loads of stall holders and cars had left. By 1030 place was half empty. Very disappointing
Had a site there selling collectibles tools, China, Crystal, Matchbox cars, Funho, Dinky etc
My daughter loved the display of the classic cars.

Hare Krishna Auckland is a peaceful sanctuary in the city. The temple is beautifully maintained, offering a serene atmosphere for prayer and meditation. The community is welcoming, and the spiritual ambiance is uplifting. The prasadam (food offering) is delicious and nourishing, making every visit fulfilling. A wonderful place to find tranquility and connect spiritually.

🪷Hare Ram Hare Ram, Ram Ram Hare Hare, Hare Krishn Hare Krishn, Krishn Krishn Hare Hare🪷 ॐ नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻❤️🚩 Last week, our family visited the Hare Krishna Centre (ISKCON) in Kumeū, a serene retreat nestled just a short drive from Auckland. As we entered the property, we were greeted by lush greenery stretching as far as the eye could see, a haven of tranquility that immediately set the tone for the day. The gentle mooing of cows, the cheerful clucks of hens, and the soft quacks of ducks created a natural symphony that resonated with the peaceful vibe of the place. Alpacas roamed gracefully in the fields, adding an exotic charm to the serene surroundings. The well-maintained garden was a feast for the senses, with vibrant flowers blooming in every hue, the fragrance of fresh blossoms wafting through the air. Birds of various species flitted from tree to tree, their melodies blending harmoniously with the environment. Walking amidst this natural beauty, we felt a deep sense of calm wash over us. The temple itself was an oasis of spirituality. As we stepped inside, the soothing chants of the Hare Krishna mantra transported us to a realm of peace and devotion. The altar, adorned with intricate decorations and deities, emanated a profound sense of divinity. Sitting there, surrounded by the sacred atmosphere, was a rejuvenating experience that touched our souls. After the prayers, we enjoyed a simple yet delicious vegetarian meal, lovingly prepared and served by the temple community. Sharing this prasad together as a family was not just nourishing but also deeply fulfilling. The day ended with a quiet stroll around the grounds, watching the animals graze and the sun set over the lush green fields. It was more than just a visit; it was a spiritual retreat that refreshed our minds, rejuvenated our spirits, and brought us closer as a family. We left the Hare Krishna Centre with hearts full of gratitude and a renewed sense of peace.

Hare Krishna temple and shool 🛕 Beautiful place to visit, come for darshan. Near is also Govardhan Hill and cows. Every morning Mangala arati starts 4.30 am. Altar open again at 7 am. Every Sunday programe with big vegetarian feast.

A Peaceful and Uplifting Experience at ISKCON Auckland I visited ISKCON Auckland today and had a truly calming and uplifting experience. The temple is surrounded by beautiful greenery, and the atmosphere is very peaceful. The deities of Sri Sri Radha-Giridhari are beautifully decorated, and the devotional chanting (kirtan) added to the spiritual energy of the place. Everyone was warm and welcoming, and I especially enjoyed the vegetarian lunch (prasadam) they served—simple, delicious, and offered with love. Whether you're spiritually inclined or just looking for a quiet, serene spot to reflect, ISKCON Auckland is definitely worth a visit.

In tranquil space, where peace resides, The Hare Krishna Centre, its beauty provides. With chants that rise, a soulful plea, For love and grace, eternally. The devotees, with hearts so pure, Spread kindness, and knowledge endure. They offer prasad, a sweet delight, A taste of bliss, morning, noon, and night. The temple bells, a gentle chime, Inviting all, to a sacred time. Where worries fade, and spirits soar, And love's embrace, forevermore. So let us join, in this sacred space, And find within, a peaceful grace. The Hare Krishna Centre, a guiding light, Illuminating souls, both day and night.

First time visit here. A very family friendly bike park gorgeous learners. This is not an adventure mountain bike park. It is a learning to ride your bike park for kids. We what for a rain day walk, so the lack of signage did not bother us. Great clean tiolets with lovely showers. Lots of parking. Highly recommended for a gentle walk or ride. Worth the trek.
A great place to walk and clear your mind. Lots of old trees around. The view all round is amazing. If you have a bike you can try the track out.
Beautiful scenery, nice playground for kids . There are some construction in the area .
Excellent fully fenced off leash dog park. Lots of room to exercise your pooch. Plenty of parking. Nice clean amenities. Also has areas for bike riding, horse riding and kids playground.

Great park for those who like a bit of everything, not a large area but still enjoyable walk that is good for those who are trying to improve or are new to fitness or have small children. Pictures speak for themselves. Very peaceful and tranquil. This place has character, i especially liked seeing the wooden carved tree, signs of an old tree house platform in the pines and the chain on the tree if the cliff above the sea, a place where life was lived:). Bit tucked out of the way great place to let your dog free in a good allocated space.

Not a lot of okay ground equipment, but what they have is different and interesting. The slide is wide and fun. So many things to spin on (seats, ropes and a tower). Two baby swings and two regular swings edge the park. Kids of all ages enjoy playing in the water feature with fountains. We took a walk on one of the trails to see some horses (petting not recommended). Heaps of fields to play on as well.
An inviting retreat nestled among calm and lush landscapes, with ponies adding to the picturesque backdrop 😍 Perfect for casual walks, morning jogs, unwinding, and a refreshing escape from screens!
Love it. Playground, many soccer fields. Short walk. There is small herb garden, and you pick some for free 😉.
A quite place to picnic. Kids maybe interested in the horses here too. The playground is too small, need to upgrade.

Wainoni Park is a sport facility in Greenhithe. In the winter the local soccer club Greenhithe FC hosts midget, junior and youth soccer across the three fields and in the summer various cricket clubs & Last Man Stands use the three artificial cricket pitches. Surrounding the fields are walkways through the park, a playground and two car parking areas of reasonable size - both of which quickly fill up on Saturday morning in winter. The park is popular for dog walkers who largely ignore the rules about keeping their pets off the fields so you'll get the occasional out of control dog. There are public toilets which can get pretty grotty from time to time and the council doesn't maintain some of the park as much as it should. The last part of the park is the Pony Club located to the North of the playing fields.

Herald "Island".... A lovely, peaceful spot to visit & enjoy a quiet sunset walk! Even on a chilly winter evening! A short, tree lined, pretty walk from the park to the pier! Just listening to the birdsong & the gentle lapping of the water! ♡ Sunset is beautiful & to be enjoyed, from any place in the world! It's a good time for quiet reflection! ..... & taking a good photograph ☆ Tx B..... 22/7/25....

What a beautiful park with calm water! My partner and I visited because we had always wanted to explore Herald Island. We were pleasantly surprised by its quiet, clean, and family-friendly vibe. Many locals bring their dogs and kids to enjoy the sunny weather. There are several beautiful photo spots where we enjoyed taking pictures. The park is very well maintained and lovely - it’s clear why it’s called Christmas Beach, as it made us quite happy. We enjoyed coffee and croissants we brought for afternoon tea while taking in the beautiful views of the sky, clouds, and water. This place created a wonderful memory for us. Public toilet, BBQ table, and wood-made playground are available here, well maintained by Auckland Council.

Love love love this little gem of a place on herald island, there is only one way in and one way out so it's not possible to get lost, enjoyed the walk and our dog just loves it there there's playground access for the kids as well as free bbq area so is a lovely place for a afternoon picnic
Quiet beach with great views. Not a white sand beach. And in low tide can look ugly. But its peaceful, has no crowds and has a BBQ. Great for quality time with the family
Nice little place to relax. Not great parking but nice to take a little walk through the village. Nice playground for kids.
note new address (166 Hurstmere rd) close to Bruce Mason Centre. Purchased a beautiful and reasonably priced painting there. Recommended!

I have bought a few pieces of art from here. Mike the owner has always been excellent. He is well informed about the specific artists and pieces of art. He also delivered one piece for me which has pride of place in our home and the focal point of conversation with visitors. I would highly recommend them.
Have to visit once a month. Have brought a variety of art styles that give us alot of pleasure. A must visit.
Bought a painting a few months ago great service. Went back only to find they've CLOSED for good. No address given as to where they have moved to or whether they are still in business. Such a shame.
Wow, amazing art! Unusual, offbeat and downright beautiful, highly recomend

This reef is a rocky area at the end of Takapuna Beach. You can surf here when the waves are good. At low tide, you can see small sea animals in the rock pools. It’s a fun place for kids and families. Volcanic rocks.

This volcanic area is super fascinating for its geological features! To be able to see where a forest of trees once stood and had lava pool around them, cool and harden leaving behind so many hollows (now rock pools) and arches is amazing. An amateur geologists dream stop!

Great for taking a stroll, relaxing, and family-friendly. The beach has a great playground, is even wheelchair accessible, and features lots of trees for shade. The toilets and changing rooms are clean, and there are lots of restaurants nearby. 👍🏼
Very sparsely populated midday on a weekday - shell beach but nbd. Water very temperate and little to no waves when we went

Dropped into Takapuna Beach to take in the ocean breeze & Latin Festival. It's a great location for something like this and free for everyone. The surf club is located next door, and if the kids need more entertainment the playground is massive and at the beach. Those looking to enjoy the view over food and drink, there is plenty to choose from on The Strand.

Awesome spot for a walk with ice cream or coffee. Beautiful views and the cliff makes a great spot for taking photos. Can use this area as the start for the Takapuna to Milford walk depending on the tides. Also has public toilets, rubbish bins and a world class all ages all abilities playground. Check water quality if going for a swim would be the only caution.

Really stunning beach. Just a few minutes from the city, with a lovely cafe and ice cream shop. Very dog friendly, big park for kids and a perfect beach for relaxing, swimming or whatever. Can get crowded at peak times but even then there’s normally plenty of room.
Beautiful view from here. You can see Rangitoto island from here. Nice walk up the hill. Maori historic site here.

Lookout towards Rangitoto and Takapuna. It's located on a short walk from the playground carpark. There are two sets of stairs but other than that the walk is easy. It's also fee mins wall accessible from Castor Bay Beach reserve. View is nice and quiet. There are benches nearby with good view of the coast.

A pleasant walk with a pretty beach below. There's a slight slope at the start of the lookout, but otherwise it's easy and accessible. Reach the small signpost. If you go right, you'll find the lookout. If you go up to the park, there's a nice viewpoint with stairs on the left. Free

The water was fantastic! Warmer, then I anticipated! Great service from both the ferry trips with Fuller360. We did the left loop of the island. We did the western loop with the crater loop too. Took us about a little over 3 hours. They estimated about 3 hours 45 mintues
Beutiful place to swim! Well worth the walk around or boat directly there
A peaceful place to spend a couple of minutes and relax.

Very small, very windy, pebbly rather than sandy, not hugely swim-friendly, BUT has a gorgeous idyllic position at the waters' edge around the island. Worth the walk from Rangitoto Wharf with a picnic and your swimmers (if you're brave in Summer, or utterly bonkers in Winter)
Nice place to visit and chill not many people. Also there is washroom nearby

Great place to stay for a few nights, sheltered from most wind if your camping. Requires a reasonable treck to get here now, now that the ferries stopped running. Some great hikes to historical sites around the campsite as well.
Quiet nothing really to see and to do a bit boring
the best attention and quality of people you will find
The Island Time 2021 event used this as the venue. Great spot for it

Beautiful little island to switch off and relax. The campsite offers a variety of places to pitch tents, including under trees. There are also some large benches to sit on. Unfortunately, the shelter does not have any seating, but it does have very clean flush toilets. Day hikes around the island as well as swimming in the shallow water are easily possible. It takes just under 90 minutes to walk to the ferry pier.

Awesome place, had a great snorkelling day with EMR 🙂 stunning walks, beautiful coast line and great place to snorkel. I would like to return and maybe camp here for a few days, the only thing I still need to figure out is where I can refill my water bottle.

Campsite is maintained often by cutting grass lawn and removing invasive pampas grass. If you are hiking from Rangitoto Island be sure to leave plenty of sunlight as the Coastal Walk track took us 3.5 hours, most of it in the dark. Lots of wild life around and pretty pebbles on the beach.
Thanks to the government we won the voucher to come here. It is really nothing we can do. Small island nothing on it, no food no water no people. Very isolated feels like a run away movie.
harder to walk than rangitoto tf?
Lovely Place, had a great time camping overnight a few months ago

While the gallery may be small, it showcases a unique and special selection of New Zealand art. The carefully curated collection ensures you will discover something truly distinctive. The staff are exceptionally friendly and knowledgeable, making the experience even more enjoyable. A hidden gem that's definitely worth a visit.
The wonderful gallery shop features high-quality ceramics, glass, jewellery, and artworks from Waiheke and around Aotearoa.

I went there with a little box of jewellery - earrings and finger rings - to have exhibited there, plus a little selection from the archives of my handmade eyewear, from strangely normal sterling silver "Looking Glasses" to optical absurda Italian acetate frames one of which I dyed lenses and frame together and called it "Rare Fruit". All are able to have your own prescription lenses fitted at Island Eyes along the road.

What an amazing Gallery 👏 Not only does the art on display excel, but also the helpful ushers who gave of her time to share what exhibition were on offer/ display on the island. I also purchased some lovely earrings from the gift shop. If you haven't been, but plan to visit the art installation, make it a priority. You won't be disappointed.

Wonderful public gallery servicing Waiheke's artists and art-lovers. The Waiheke Art Gallery skillfully serves the aspirations of Waiheke's emergent artists while also showcasing the work of established contemporary New Zealand artists. A real treat for visitors to the island.

The rail dog is a hidden treasure of Waiheke. It's a bit of a trek to visit but well worth it. A tad disappointed there isn't a visitors centre or gift shop - would have loved to take a souvenir home. Not to be missed!
100% Rail Dog. No additives.
Product came as described. 10/10 would order again. Seller was prompt and helpful
I havent been there but so far it looks like a good boy
Good dog would dog again

A great bike ride all the way around the island with lots of stops at all the base. The bike rental place gave us a map and gave us all the information we needed and all the top spots to stop at. He made everything so simple. The bikes are well equipped with a dry bag and lock, and they are good quality bikes. The pedal assist helps you with even the steepest mountains. This is way better than the bus get out there and explore.

Great bikes, amazing staff, perfect location. They make this the easiest place to rent from, right in the ferry terminal. The staff was so helpful, they make sure you have all the info and gear you need. I highly recommended using this company. I did the Man O War tour and it was such an incredible way to see the island.

Firstly shout out to Max for being what was essentially our guide even though we only met him at the beginning to hire the bikes. He was full of information and extremely friendly! My wife and I tackled the 5 bays ride and had a wonderful afternoon filled with views and great dining. It was a great ride and the new app they have was seriously helpful (even gave us pep talks when we hit the hills hahaha) it worked offline so we were able to save battery and it was full of information regarding what we were coming up to and what was around the area. I think the island itself let us down more on our journey just as some of the winery locations weren’t actually signed that well so that’s where the app saved us. Thanks again Max and E-Bike Hire, would 100% recommend the cruisy 5 bays self guided tour and stopping at The Heke for food and drinks.

Fantastic service from the lads. Only caught Pablos name, but was very impressed with both of the lads.Information on route was spot on. Bike was great, no issues with 60k round the island (no charge needed) highly recommend them. I used the new app form the lads and it worked really well!

We had a fantastic experience with eRide Waiheke! We did the self-guided e-bike tour, and it was incredibly smooth from start to finish. After scanning the provided QR code, we followed a thoughtfully planned Google Maps route that took us past stunning beaches, vineyards, and scenic lookouts. The bikes were well-maintained and came with helmets, panniers, and everything we needed. Some of the uphill sections required a bit of gear shifting finesse, and using the "Level 3" pedal assist strategically helped a lot. Definitely felt like the right balance of exercise and ease. Being able to explore the island at our own pace made the whole day feel relaxed and enjoyable. Pickup at the Matiatia ferry terminal was super convenient, and the staff were friendly and helpful. Highly recommend this to anyone visiting Waiheke who wants to get off the beaten path and see the island in a fun, eco-friendly way!
This place is incredible. So many historical musical instruments, wonderful tour and fantastic atmosphere. You can actually play the pianos which was a great experience. Very highly recommend

A fantastic hour and a quarter with Rosemary at the Museum. We saw and heard some amazing instruments and heard the story of Lloyd and Joan. What a love story. We exhort all who visit the island make time and arrange a visit. Loved it.

Would have loved to go and visit. But it was closed on king's birthday. A bit weird as this is a holiday day and the day you would probably atrack most people so for a tourist type thing it's a bit weird to be closed on a day most people can do tourist things.
Very helpful and interesting guy showed us all of the instruments and how they worked and what make each one unique. Definitely recommend, fantastic!

I recommend that all music lovers stop here. They have a large collection of pianos, accordions, a xylophone, and more. The employees are talented and will play for you and will also give you a chance to play yourself :-)

A nice green area featuring some very old Pohutukawa trees just above Oneroa village and bay. Some interesting sculptures and a small commemoration plaque and flag pool. A good place to relax out of the bustle of the areas closer to the water.

Nice spacious park for open activities and dog walking. Unfortunately not the best view of the waters below which would make this park top notch, but it does have some cool statues and a small floral garden.
Yah not too bad of a spot but not all that much to see. There are some neat benches but overall more of a non-beach picnic area if you didn't want to walk down to the beach.
Nice quiet park with a few good sculptures to see. Good for a walk

Great park to stroll , with a small 5 minute walk bush track which is flat and always quiet, rarely see anybody on it. Has the bee garden with various shrubs and plants , ... lavender etc. There are 5 or 6 sculptures to see as you walk through the park. My favorite are 2 carved Rocks. One is a Taniwha (water monster in the Maori folklore) the other is a few metres away another Maori inspired rock carving a beautifully detailed seat for two. My absolute favorite place to sit and take in the islands fresh air , with little or no disturbances as it's off the track slightly. I'm there day or night, has a magical spiritual vibe. The park is on the edge of the village so getting there is with no effort. I have only one little adverse comment, which is a tree with it's trunk growing across part of the path , and because I like to wear a cap when walking I have failed to see it , resulting in 2 hits to the head on 2 separate occasions. After 2 times, I guess I became aware from then so there has never been a 3rd time. People I have seen along the way are very friendly, I can say a 100 percent track record for passerby greetings , having saying that the people are few. Apart from my 2 head ,,(I admit they were my own fault) hits it's the safest park I have ever frequented. I recommend this park especially because of it's serenity and peacefulness. A nice little getaway from the sometimes very crowded village.
Epic welcome from Waiheke!! Love our Beachbathers mugs & caps from the shop 🌟
Epic. Lovely little photo shoot to finish off a great day. Cool shop next door too
Perfect spot for a quick insta pic and a souvenir. The guy behind it is an icon of Waiheke!
Easy to find and a cool shop next door that’s sells great souvenirs!
Can’t believe it’s free, and the shop next door has some neat little items too!!!
A small but gorgeous gallery in the main village with wall sculptures by local artists, cleverly done art with a calming vibe.

This is a small, uninspired museum. It is free to New Zealandrrs, but the $20 per person for non-residents isn't worth it. The architecture is lovely, but you can see that from the outside. The surrounding park and plantings are well worth the visit.

We spent a lot of money on a spectacular piece of artwork a few years ago when we last visited. It has pride of place in our house here in UK. We would certainly visit again next time we are in New Zealand.
Brilliant works in the gallery, I’m a great fan of their bird pattern wall pieces that are bursting with character.
A place of calm, understated elegance and step away from main street.

Anchored overnight here during a bout of very strong south to south west wind. Good holding on a sandy bottom and relatively sheltered. Easy access to long sandy beach and the shopping precinct of Oneroa. This is normally a busy anchorage with good depth up close to the shore.
Oneroa beach is one of the better beaches on the island. On a nice day, its north east side is calm, tranquil and perfect for kids to swim. Very close to the main road and shops as well.
Not so many boats right now zzo reasonay tidy and relative safe to swim
Best whale watching experience ever.
A small island suitable for vacation, it is recommended to make a plan in advance

A wonderful walk for a sunny day, its a lot of steps though so take plenty of water. There are several benches along the walk to the start od this track but when you get on this track its pretty much steps and pathway. Lovely when you get down there though, lots of rock pools to look in with many snails and barnacles to look at. Love it. Also there is no access along from the beach so when you go down all those steps you do have to come back up.

As the name suggests it’s a good fishing spot for Snapper and even Kingfish. But it’s also a great hidden area for swimming (rock jumping) and snorkeling during mid to high tide. To access the site park at the end of Newton rd and follow the path to the coast. There are a lot of stairs and it’s worth bringing study sole shoes to climb the rocks to get to the swimming area. It’s also a good idea to bring water shoes to get in and out of the water to avoid the oysters. This is not a beach so don’t expect a sandy area, it’s rugged with lots of rocks and tidal channels. Also to correct something previously stated in another review, the track is not muddy in the summer even after a good downpour.

my hubby decided to check this place as it is at the edge of the beach, turns out the pathway going in was muddy until we reached a clear stairway going down to the rocky area.. my son was fine with long walks then he was disappointed when we reached as there’s no way he can play in the water (he loves beach)..so in the end we left and as we walked back, my son slipped and cried as the footpath is muddy.. I will not recommend this place with kids.
Highly recommend to come and check this place out, i think from there u can see a very good view of the coast, and ocean with different vibes.

Good viewpoint, but the council really needs to cut grass near it . bushes are overgrown . When u reach all the way to end to see viewpoint, hardly any space to stand to click photo. Need little deck or something to stand on or to put your camera steady.

This is the second visit I have made to the gardens and still I get the feelings of calm and peace whilst I’m there. One cannot help but slow down and enjoy the many, well thought out places to rest and take in the surrounding views, listen to the birds and breathe in the fresh clean air. This garden has evolved with compassion and love from all the people who have had a part in its creation. Please visit and give yourself more time than you think you need. This place is special and so very good for your soul. Thank you Sacred Blessing Sanctuary Garden.

Gorgeous garden. I've been to a lot but never to one as put together and taken care of as well as this one. Flowers were gorgeous, cool statues, so many super clean and cute places to sit with gorgeous views. Loads of Tui around and plenty of vege that are either donated to food banks or for staff to take home to eat

My wife and I stumbled across this gem while touring Waiheke Island with an E-bike rental. It was my second visit to the island and her first, but we were both able to experience this place of beauty for the first time together. To be in a place as beautiful as the island, just to walk down a hill and be mesmerized by something so incredible. An amazing place run by incredible and kind-hearted people. A labor of love 20 years in the making turned into a magnificent garden in-tune with nature, yet beautifully set-up for tours through the entire place with many places to stop and pinch yourself to make sure you aren't dreaming! We cannot recommend stopping by and visiting this gem more! Thank you guys so much for adding such a special place to our honeymoon!

Beautiful garden to visit. We basically had the whole garden to ourselves because we visited off season but it was still worth it! Alan was very knowledgeable about the garden and showed us the monarch nursery and how they make compost. Very cool place to visit and would love to come again during hatching season.

Such a beautiful, tranquil garden. We were recommended it by a friend of one of the gardeners in the UK and were so glad we made the time to visit. Tui birds flit about the garden and sit in the trees making their wonderful, exotic calls.
Beautiful Place
Loved this spot . Waiheke Island is a must stop when visiting Auckland.
Awesome MTB trails, well maintained and clean. Water, repair, and site map stations are installed in the tracks. Staff are very accommodating and friendly

pulse racing trails, berms, jumps, hacks and treks. Trails for all levels of fitness. Hire bikes available or bring your own hard tail or full suspension. I have the best times riding out here, and there are no cars to contend with when your riding. Get off the streets and onto the trails!

Awesome bike park with something for everyone. I'm a beginner and found the grade 2 tracks suited my skill level. Some little challenges on the way but definitely manageable. You can hire bikes. Bring lunch and snacks with you but there's a water station, fruit ice cream and coffee available too. We took with us a 7 year old, 5 year old and 3 year old. Plenty of families around as well as experienced riders. We had a great day all for $40.
5/5 trails are well maintained, great vibes. I’m a regular so I’m biased.

Good place to have fun on your mtb any time of year. Trails different grade, service station on site🚲Ride from dawn to dusk No doubds 5 star mtb park I would add an extra 5 stars for concrete (dust free) driveway down to carpark 😉

Fantastic experience for locals and tourists alike. The pricing is very fair considering what’s involved. You’re given a fair choice of courses to partake in to suit all ages. The courses are various, which keeps it interesting no matter your skill level or confidence with heights. The courses were well-maintained, and the breathtaking scenery of the forest added to the adventure. It was a perfect way to spend the day outdoors, challenging myself and having fun. I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a thrilling adventure in a beautiful setting!

This place was really fun😆 and this place rocks. My daughter and her friends did the zip lining adventure. Beautiful traditional market in an open field like setting. Great food, crafts and live music and entertainment. Parking is easy on paddock close by.

Really nice market with heaps of different vendors. Great location and good vibes. We always go early about 9.30am (market opens at 10am) - otherwise it's really difficult to find a carpark. Beautiful waterfall you wouldn’t expect to find so close to you main road. It was a nice place to check out after having a picnic at the nearby reserve.

Lovely walk to waterfalls. Be aware, unlike me, that there are paths on each side of the Lucas River that lead to the waterfalls. Today, I wandered through Albany, Auckland, as the final days of autumn gently unfolded around me. The air carried a soft chill—just enough to hint that winter was near—yet the world was still wrapped in the warm tones of the season. The path was scattered with fallen leaves in shades of rust, gold, and amber, forming a natural tapestry beneath my feet. With every step, there was a soft crunch—a quiet rhythm marking the changing season. Trees stood tall, some nearly bare, others still holding onto their last bursts of color, as if reluctant to let go of autumn’s charm. By a calm body of water, ducks glided smoothly, their reflections rippling in the gentle light. A small group of pigeons lifted into the sky, wings catching the breeze, circling above before settling again. There was a quiet harmony in their motion, a peaceful joy in simply existing within this changing world. Among the trees, a few stood out—perhaps fruit trees—displaying the final blaze of autumn’s fire. Their leaves, bright red and golden yellow, were scattered in circles around their trunks. It was striking to see such vivid colors resting on fresh green grass, as if the earth was celebrating one last burst of color before winter's hush. It was a moment of stillness and motion all at once—leaves drifting, birds flying, water flowing. Everything felt alive, yet calm. As I walked, I felt grounded, reminded that even in the quiet turn of seasons, beauty is everywhere, waiting to be noticed.

Love this little spot for a picnic on a hot day! Kell Park has everything you need and more: plenty of shade, public toilets, ample parking and pushchair/wheelchair accessible pathways. Dogs are allowed off leash year round (although mind the free range chickens!) Albany library is just alongside so perfect to grab a book and read in the shade. There is a small playground (suitable for younger children) in the main park - or follow the pathway in either direction for a short bush walk to the big slide and flying fox (flying fox was out of order when we visited Jan 2024). For older children there isn’t a lot to do here - though the flying fox if working would be a good draw. We visit this park fairly frequently and it is never busy.

Here’s a polished Google review for Sherwood Reserve, written in a balanced and engaging tone: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ A Hidden Gem on the North Shore! Sherwood Reserve is one of those places that makes you feel like you've discovered a secret oasis in the middle of suburbia. It’s got everything – a beautiful duck pond, shaded walking paths, a cool wooden playground for the kids, and plenty of grassy areas to picnic or kick a ball around. What I love most is how peaceful it is. Even on a busy day, there’s enough space to find your own quiet corner. The native trees and little bridges give it a storybook vibe – perfect for strolls, drawing inspiration, or just letting the kids explore. Bonus: there's usually plenty of parking nearby, and it’s just a short walk to Browns Bay shops if you want to grab a coffee or bite after. Browns Bay Reserve is a fantastic coastal park located on Auckland’s North Shore, offering a great mix of relaxation and recreational activities. With its spacious grassy areas, scenic beachfront, and well-maintained amenities, it is an ideal spot for families, fitness enthusiasts, and anyone looking to enjoy the outdoors. One of the main highlights of the reserve is its stunning beach, which features golden sand and calm waters perfect for swimming, paddleboarding, or just relaxing by the shore. The beachfront walkway provides beautiful ocean views, making it a popular spot for walkers and joggers. For families, the reserve includes a well-equipped playground that keeps children entertained, as well as picnic tables and barbecue facilities that make it easy to spend the entire day here. There is also plenty of open space for playing sports or simply unwinding. The area is surrounded by a range of cafés and restaurants, allowing visitors to enjoy a meal or coffee with a view. The nearby Browns Bay town center offers convenience with its shops and local markets. Parking is generally available but can get busy during weekends and summer months. Additionally, public toilets and changing facilities are clean and easily accessible. Overall, Browns Bay Reserve is a perfect destination for a relaxing day by the beach, whether you’re looking for a peaceful retreat or an active day out. It offers something for everyone and is definitely worth a visit.
Really nice, clean and tidy, with a beautiful view. Lots of cafes around too. Amazing playground.
Picnic tables, free BBQs, skate park, playground, public toilets & showers. Beautiful beach, great shops and eateries in the area. One of my favourite places on the North Shore!

Parakai Springs pools in Parakai, New Zealand is a fantastic destination for families looking for a fun and relaxing day out. The pools feature both indoor and outdoor options, with warm pools, hydro slides, and plenty of amenities to keep everyone entertained. The main pool at Parakai Springs is around 20 degrees, making it a comfortable temperature for swimming and playing. There is also a warmer indoor pool that sits at 30 degrees, with an open roof, which is perfect for those who want to take a break from the sun. The hydro slides are a huge hit with visitors of all ages and provide hours of entertainment for kids and adults alike. The facilities at Parakai Springs are top-notch, with plenty of tables and outdoor BBQ areas available for visitors to use. The staff is friendly and the environment is safe and welcoming, making it a great option for families with young children. The shop on-site is also a great place to grab a snack or a souvenir. Overall, Parakai Springs pools is an awesome destination for families looking to enjoy some time in the water and have some fun. With its warm and comfortable pools, exciting hydro slides, and great facilities, it's a perfect place to spend a day. The spring water is a great addition and the fact it is a safe environment with friendly staff makes it an even more enjoyable experience for all.

Had an amazing night for a paranormal investigation with Paranormal NZ and like minded people in April (totally forgot about leaving a review here$). Not too much happening during that night but I loved the atmosphere, those old historic buildings and the objects displayed inside them.

Amazing guide just for 5 dollars. Got shown around by one of the amazing volunteers and learnt alot more about the history in the area,historical figures that I never knew about in the area and how poorly the crown treated the Maori in the area and further up north.

The museum was very interesting, there was a lovely office lady who’d seen us walk in she and popped her head out said ‘Hello’ and said we were welcome to joined the guided tour that had just started. I’m looking forward to returning because I missed part of tour so didn’t hear the story about it. I’m guessing the back room was the formal parlour where they entertained visitors with tea and scones - or maybe I’m getting to carried away. I had purchased a couple of books ‘ Voygeering men’ and a book about Women of pioneering families. So to pop into the museum was a must. I also met a lady whose family was a descendent of the Mcleods family - so it was extra special. The history of Helensville is very interesting. I was born and raised in West Auckland. The garden out front is lovely, and the ladies were very welcoming. Oh I should’ve taken more photos, but these two items were the ones - I had no idea what they were.

I finally did it—I skydived! And I couldn’t have asked for a better team to guide me through such an unforgettable experience. And of course, a gentle shoutout to the lovely ground crew, Laura and Glenn, whose warm smiles and guidance helped me feel ready from the ground up. And to Max, our wonderful driver—thank you for getting us there and back safely with such a chill vibe. You’re awesome! This was more than just a skydive—it was an experience I’ll carry for life. Nothing better than jumping out of a plane on your birthday. That’s exactly what I did and what a crazy but thrilling adventure!! Huge thanks to the ground crew Max & Glen for the kind welcome. The best experience ever!! 🪂

I had an amazing experience and I know this won't be my last time doing this! Max picked us up from the hotel on time and he told us we'll have about 45 minutes until we reach the place. Glenn welcomed us once we were there and he was the one who showed us safety videos and took our preference for how high we'd like to go up and what package we'd like to get for photos and videos. My recommendation is the ultimate package! You won't regret it! 😍 I was paired to jump with Aaron and Matthew was going with us to film the whole experience from another perspective (Aaron was filming too). On the way to the plane I talked with Aaron to get to know him better and he told me he has been doing this for 20 years! My confidence immediately went up and I knew I was in safe hands up there! We were sitting right next to the pilot so I was able to learn some things- specifically how skydivers get notified about the time they should jump. The free fall felt incredible! It lasted 60 seconds and after that, the parachute was pulled and we could enjoy smooth ride back to the base with amazing views around us! I am thankful for the amazing team I got!

Had the most amazing time skydiving in Auckland and I have to give a huge shoutout to the incredible team who made the entire experience seamless and unforgettable! From the ground crew — Alex, Joe, and Matthew — everything was organized and well-explained. The briefing was clear and reassuring, and they walked us through every step so we knew exactly what to expect. Registration and payment were super easy too, with the option to top up on-site for jump height or to add photos and videos (which I highly recommend!). Special thanks to Jacob, my jump instructor, who was an absolute gem. He was so patient and kind, answered all my questions, and made me feel totally at ease. I was a bit nervous but he kept the energy light and positive the whole time. Also, props to Sam, our pilot, for a smooth takeoff and flight. Would 100% recommend this team if you’re thinking of skydiving in NZ. Safe, professional, and such a fun crew to jump with!

To all the crew at SKYDIVE AUCKLAND Kia ora! Well, where do I start? I’m not sure what I expected but one thing I know is that others will tell you all sorts of things that may happen and what it may be like. Jumping out of ‘a perfectly good aeroplane, why would you do that’ was a comment that was mentioned? Firstly I experienced the adrenaline rush of the free fall - highly recommend jumping at18000 feet! Then you are just flying around the sky taking it all in. When the parachute was pulled - again what can I say, felt like I was being sucked up even higher into the sky/atmosphere. Then unfortunately came the landing and all to soon it was over. I cannot thank you all enough for this ‘Wow’ of an experience. It would have to be the most exciting/memorable/incredible experiences of my life. Certainly, no regrets and will do it all again. I re-live the moment often. They say that tomorrow is not promised so JUST DO IT and never look back! As Arnold said, ‘I’ll be back’. Highly recommend the Ultimate Package! Charmaine! 7/7/2025

Very busy and had to kick someone off a table who believed eventhough she was watching kids skiing she could keep a 6-seat table by leaving a water bottle on it. We had lunch and left, she was still watching kids. Food was good and it was the first time my wife had been there.

"An Unforgettable Day at Auckland Adventure Park!" We had an absolutely fantastic day at Auckland Adventure Park! We purchased four Ultimate Passes from Bookme for just $20 each, which was an incredible deal for all the activities included. The park is conveniently located in North Shore, Auckland, making it easy to reach and perfect for families or thrill-seekers. The rides open at 11 a.m., giving us plenty of time to explore the park. We started in the kids' area, where our little ones loved the planes, carousel, pirate ship, and a fun playground. There’s also a 4D cinema, where we enjoyed a rollercoaster movie with 3D glasses and seat movement—a fun experience for everyone. The heart of the park, Area 51, serves as both the check-in area and a kitchen. We grabbed lunch here, and the food was delicious and reasonably priced. To get to the main attractions like the Shooting Star ride, luge, and dual zip line, you can either take a short uphill walk or hop on a comfortable Mitsubishi Rosa bus. The driver was very friendly and added to the great atmosphere of the day. The luge was super fast—definitely quicker than the one in Rotorua—and it had bicycle-like brakes for control, making it an exhilarating but safe ride. The dual zip line was another highlight, offering a fast-paced, adrenaline-filled experience that we absolutely loved! In the middle of the day, we experienced a heavy downpour of rain, but it cleared up in just 20 minutes. The brief rainstorm actually added to the day, making the rides feel even more refreshing and fun once it passed. It’s all part of the adventure! The Ultimate Pass gave us unlimited access to all these activities, and for $50, it’s absolutely worth it. We could ride as much as we wanted, which really made the day special. Overall, we had an amazing time at Auckland Adventure Park and we’ll definitely be back every year. Whether you're visiting with kids or looking for some thrilling experiences, this park has something for everyone. Highly recommend it!

Oakley Creek Falls is an impressive six-meter-high waterfall - one of the two urban waterfalls in Auckland city (the other one, Lucas Creek Falls, is in Albany). It is on Auckland’s longest urban stream, which starts from the Hillsborough/Mt Roskill area and meets the sea at the Waterview area of Waitematā Harbour. Oakley Creek is also known as Te Auaunga, and the abundance of native and exotic flora and fauna makes it an important natural habitat in the central city for many species. Oakley Creek is also home to the endangered New Zealand longfin eel, so fishing of any kind is not permitted on the stream. Additionally, swimming is also not advised due to poor water quality, and there is a permanent public health warning in place against swimming. Oakley falls can be accessed from Great North Road, between the cycle overbridge and Blockhouse Bay Road (opposite Heron Park). It can also be accessed from the Unitec campus precinct, but due to ongoing heavy construction work (2024), access road is not clearly visible and can be confusing. This waterfall was part of the Oakley Stream track, which had a span of 4.5 km. However, after Cyclone Gabrielle in 2023, the track is now limited to less than 2 km as several bridges have been washed away. There is a viewing platform, boardwalk, and a bench, but they are in bad shape due to cyclone damage as well as graffiti vandalism. It is a bit unfortunate that you may find heaps of rubbish, plastics, tyres, and cyclone debris along the creek that have not been attended or cleaned up for a long while. It looks that once highly active 'Friends of Oakley Creek,' which was established in 2004, is not as active anymore.
